Repo: /Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/M-VAVE_FM-1 (personal knowledge base + own firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 pocket synth, built on the `third_party/fm1-base` submodule). Read-only research, "very thorough".

I am evaluating whether a vocabulary-flashcard firmware app with spoken English words (tiny on-device text-to-speech, or pre-encoded speech) is feasible. I need hard facts with file:line citations:

1. Hardware: MCU (JieLi part number), CPU clock, RAM size (and how much an app gets), flash size (1 MiB) and how much is free for app data / app code, LCD resolution and colour depth, audio output path (DAC? sample rate? speaker/headphone), buttons/keys layout. Look in docs/hardware/, docs/dev/, third_party/fm1-base docs/README, and fm1-base headers.
2. fm1-base API surface relevant to: (a) audio — can an app play arbitrary PCM samples / a sample buffer / a synth voice, at what rate, any audio callback; how does firmware/morse produce its tone (find the code); (b) display — text drawing, fonts available (any CJK/Chinese font? font sizes), images; (c) storage — APP_STORE_MAP in app.h, max sizes, how morse persists data; (d) host link — USB MIDI / BLE (firmware/common/hostlink), SysEx, max throughput, how host/morse sends text to the device. (e) can an app embed large read-only data (e.g. a 200 KB word list) in the .fwsc, and is there a code-size limit.
3. firmware/morse: summarize architecture — learn.c flash cards (is there spaced repetition / Leitner / scheduling already?), how cards are stored, how the host sends text (host/morse/PROTOCOL.md). Also docs/dev/morse.md design notes. List reusable modules (firmware/common: hostlink, ledfx, chime).
4. docs/dev/index.md: current blockers for building/flashing own firmware (has any own build been flashed? is `just fw-build` working?).
5. Any existing mention anywhere in the repo of TTS, speech, voice, samples, Anki, vocabulary, flashcards, SRS.

Report concisely with file paths and line numbers; quote key numbers verbatim. Do not modify anything.

For each, give: code size, RAM needs, data size, CPU needs, licence, output quality, whether it has been ported to small MCUs (ESP32, RP2040, STM32, AVR, Cortex-M0), and a link to the repo.

Candidates to check (add others you find):

- eSpeak / espeak-ng on ESP32 (e.g. pschatzmann/arduino-espeak-ng), its RAM/flash needs; formant synthesis; licence GPL-3

````text
1	# 接口與連線
2	
3	## 各接口能做什麼
4	
5	| 接口 | 能做 | 不能做 |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| **USB-C** | 充電、USB MIDI in/out、韌體更新、USB audio（依韌體）、自訂 HID 裝置（依韌體）、USB host（只有少數韌體，見下） | 供電給接上的裝置 |
8	| **3.5 mm TRS MIDI IN** | 接收其他設備的 note、CC、clock | 不是 MIDI OUT |
9	| **3.5 mm 音訊輸出** | 立體聲類比輸出到耳機、mixer、錄音介面 | 不是 audio in，也不是 MIDI |
10	| **Bluetooth MIDI** | 硬體本身有無線電（SoC 內建 Bluetooth 與 WiFi）。原廠、CTL-1、Melodee、RemoteFM1、ChoralRoot 會用 | 要韌體開啟才有。SLOOP 不支援，它不開無線電。Agent Deck 也不支援：它的基底 Dinghy 完全沒有藍牙程式 `[上游]` |
11	
12	## 沒有音訊輸入：能不能當 sampler { #no-audio-in }
13	
14	FM-1 **沒有任何類比音訊輸入**，沒有麥克風，3.5 mm 孔只是輸出。所以不能像一般 sampler 那樣把線接進來錄。`[上游]`
15	
16	聲音要進到 FM-1，只能**從電腦或手機用數位方式送進去**，而且要韌體支援：
17	
18	| 方式 | 例子 | 狀態 |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| 從網頁上傳 sample 檔案 | SLOOP 的 [Web Editor](../firmware/sloop/web-editor.md)（4 個 slot，可以丟長錄音進去 CHOP）、官方 Workbench、Mini-Grain、ECHOFIELD 的 companion web app | `[上游]` |
21	| 讓 FM-1 當 USB 音效卡的**輸出端**，收主機播的聲音 | CTL-1（iPad 的聲音會從 FM-1 播出來，我實測過）、FM1 Audio Router | `[實機]` CTL-1 |
22	| 收主機的 USB 音訊並錄成 sample | ECHOFIELD 的說明寫 "your own samples (or recorded over USB)"，但沒說是哪個方向 | 沒查證 `[調研]` |
23	
24	所以「手機或網頁 + FM-1」的組合可以做到 sampler 的效果：在手機或電腦上錄好、剪好，再上傳到支援 sample 的韌體。ChoralRoot 做不到，它的聲音全是合成的，沒有 sample 引擎（GRAIN 引擎是對它自己生成的素材做 granular，不能載入外部 sample），USB 音訊也只有輸出到主機的方向。`[上游]` `[實機]`
25	
26	Firmware Hub 上找 sampler 類韌體：在 [catalog](https://thefirmwarehub.com/) 搜尋 sample、granular。
27	
28	## USB-C：device，不是 host
29	
30	FM-1 是 USB device。USB 鍵盤直接插在 FM-1 上不會動，因為兩邊都是 device，中間需要一個 host：電腦、手機或 USB MIDI host box。
31	
32	**例外（更正 2026-11-17）**：ChoralRoot 0.31 起有 **Options → USB Host**，打開後 USB-C 變成 USB MIDI host，可以直接接一台 USB MIDI 鍵盤，或用一條 USB-C 線把兩台 FM-1 互接。限制：FM-1 不供電，鍵盤要透過有供電的 hub 或 OTG 轉接頭；只支援 full-speed；開著時電腦、USB audio、更新都不能用；每次開機都回到一般 device 模式，不會存。`[上游]`（[release notes](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ChoralRootFM1/blob/main/docs/releases/0.31.md)）其他韌體預設仍是 device。
33	
34	反過來，電腦對 FM-1 可以做的事很多：
35	
36	- 接收琴鍵與旋鈕送出的 MIDI note / CC。
37	- 送 MIDI 回去控制合成器或 sequencer。
38	- 用支援 USB audio 的韌體直接數位錄音。
39	- 透過雙向 MIDI / SysEx 自訂螢幕內容、LED 狀態與 host 控制協定（Agent Deck 就是這樣做的）。
40	- 用自訂韌體讓 FM-1 變成 HID 鍵盤 / 滑鼠（Trireme）。
41	
42	注意不同韌體的 MIDI mapping 不同。不能假設每個實體按鍵在原廠韌體下都會送出獨立事件。`[調研]`
43	
44	## 兩台 FM-1 互連 { #two-units }
45	
46	有沒有辦法讓兩台 FM-1 直接互傳？硬體和 fm1-base 都留了路，但 2026-11-17 為止沒有找到有人在兩台實機上做過的紀錄。`[上游]` `[調研]`
47	
48	| 方式 | 怎麼接 | 限制 | 狀態 |
49	|---|---|---|---|
50	| **藍牙直連** | 一台開 `ble_central = true` 去掃描、連上另一台（它以 `FM-1 XXXX` 廣播 BLE MIDI） | fm1-base 自己的 BLE stack（`ble_stack = "own"`）一次只能有一條藍牙 MIDI 連線，連著另一台時電腦就不能走藍牙（USB 還可以）；JieLi 的 stack 可以兩條同時連，但會丟掉收到的 SysEx。central 的 connection interval 是 11.25 ms | fm1-base 只在模擬的無線電上測過（`docs/bt/BLE-DEVICES-DESIGN.md`、`tests/bt/ble_f2f_test.c`），沒有在兩台實機上測過 `[上游]` |
51	| **USB-C 線** | 一台切成 USB host（fm1-base `usb_host = true`，或 ChoralRoot 的 Options → USB Host） | FM-1 的 USB 口不供電；兩台都有電池，所以被接的那台可能不需要，但 FM-1 在沒有 VBUS 時會不會被列舉，沒有文件。fm1-base 的 host 模式收不到 SysEx，也不送 SysEx，note 和 CC 可以；它的 host 輸出路徑還沒在實機驗證 | ChoralRoot 0.31 的 release notes 說可以用 USB-C 線把兩台互接；[MIDIMON](https://github.com/ignis32/midimonitor_fm1) 的作者說接的裝置要有自己的電源（「例如另一台 FM-1」），並用它 debug 另一台 `[上游]` |
52	| **經過電腦** | 兩台都接電腦（USB 或藍牙），由電腦轉送；也可以經網路，例如 Vail | 要有電腦 | 最可靠 |
53	| TRS MIDI | — | FM-1 只有 MIDI IN，沒有 OUT，做不到雙向 | 不可行 |
54	
55	要讓同一個程式走得過以上每一條路，最穩的是只用 note on / off 這類一般 MIDI 訊息，不要依賴 SysEx。自製的[摩斯電碼機](../dev/morse.md)就是這樣設計：線上只傳按鍵的按下與放開。
56	
57	## TRS MIDI IN
58	
59	需要 **TRS-to-DIN MIDI 轉接線**。沒聲音時試另一種型式（Type A / Type B）。
60	
61	SLOOP 下的 channel 對應：
62	
63	| MIDI channel | 播放 |
64	|---|---|
65	| 1、2、3 | synth track 1、2、3 |
66	| 10 | drum track |
67	| 其他 | 目前選取的 track |
68	
69	可以在 GLO → MIDI 改。MIDI clock in 可從 USB 或 TRS 進來（GLO → SYSTEM → SYNC）。
70	
71	## USB audio（SLOOP）
72	
73	SLOOP 下 FM-1 同時是一個名為 **"Felucca"** 的 USB audio 輸入：44.1 或 48 kHz、16-bit stereo、class compliant，不需要 driver。錄到的是 master 輸出，跟耳機聽到的一樣。MIDI、Web Editor、installer 都走同一條線。
74	
75	- 音量：按住 `HOME` 進選單 → **USB AUDIO**。`MASTER` 跟著 master 旋鈕；`FULL` 是固定滿音量，適合沒有輸入增益的錄音介面。
76	- 安裝後第一次要拔插一次，電腦才會重新辨識成 MIDI + audio 裝置。
77	
78	## 用電腦接收 MIDI 的最小範例
79	
80	確認電腦看到的 MIDI port（需要 `pip install mido python-rtmidi`）：
81	
82	```python
83	import mido
84	
85	print(mido.get_input_names())
86	with mido.open_input(mido.get_input_names()[0]) as port:
87	    for msg in port:
88	        print(msg)
89	```
90	
91	這是通用的 `mido` 用法，不是某個上游專案的指令。port 名稱依韌體而定。
92

````text
1	# Flash 配置圖
2	
3	FM-1 的 flash 是 1 MiB，分成 256 個 4 KiB 的 sector。誰把什麼放在哪裡，決定了換韌體時什麼會留下、什麼會被蓋掉。這頁把各個來源的說法和我自己備份的比對放在一起。
4	
5	## 總覽
6	
7	| 位址 | 內容 | 來源 |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| `0x00000`–`0x03FFF` | **boot head**：bootloader 與 boot 設定（16 KiB）。壞了就開不了機 | `[上游]` M-Flasher、Unbricker |
10	| `0x04000`–`0x92FFF` | **韌體區**。多數韌體（原廠 V15、SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1）佔這段 | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的寫入計畫 |
11	| `0x93000`–`0xE8FFF` | 原廠 V15 的**設定區**。社群韌體也把資料放在這裡面 | `[上游]` |
12	| `0xE9000` | Bluetooth 資料（配對） | `[上游]` |
13	| `0xEA000`–`0xFBFFF` | 原廠音色（factory voices） | `[上游]` |
14	| `0xFC000`–`0xFEFFF` | M-Flasher 的圖上標為 free；Felucca 系拿來放全域設定 | `[實機]` |
15	| `0xFF000`–`0xFFFFF` | key / MAC，裝置自己的資料 | `[上游]` |
16	
17	M-Flasher 的 flash map 用顏色標的就是這些：BOOT `00–03`、FIRMWARE `04–92`、SETTINGS `93–E8`、PAIRINGS `E9`、SOUNDS `EA–FB`、free `FC–FE`、MAC `FF`。
18	
19	## 韌體區不一定只到 `0x92FFF`
20	
21	| 韌體 | 佔用範圍 | 來源 |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| SLOOP 2.8.5、Agent Deck 0.7、CTL-1 1.0.3 | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入到 `0x8FFFF`） | `[實機]` |
24	| Conductor 0.1（自製，fm1-base） | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入 `0x04000`–`0x8EFFF`、`0x91000`–`0x91FFF`） | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：140 sectors |
25	| Morse 0.1 / 0.2（自製，fm1-base） | `0x04000`–`0x92FFF`（實際寫入：Conductor 0.3 → 0.1 是 `0x04000`–`0x21FFF`，0.1 → 0.2 是 `0x04000`–`0x23FFF`） | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：30、32 sectors |
26	| **ChoralRoot 0.41** | `0x04000`–**`0x9EFFF`** | `[實機]` M-Flasher 的計畫：152 sectors |
27	| **原廠 V16** | 到 **`0xA8FFF`** | `[上游]` Unbricker |
28	
29	超出 `0x92FFF` 的韌體會直接蓋掉別人放在 `0x93000` 之後的資料。
30	
31	## Felucca 系韌體的資料位置
32	
33	Felucca、SLOOP、ChoralRoot 以及 Dinghy、fm1-base 系的韌體大多沿用同一套位址 `[上游]`：
34	
35	| 位址 | 內容 |
36	|---|---|
37	| `0x97000` 起 | project（曲子） |
38	| `0x9F000` | SLOOP 的 autosave（和 ChoralRoot 的 FM6 bank 是同一個物件編號） |
39	| `0xA0000` 起 | samples |
40	| `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF` | 自製 [Morse](../dev/morse.md#flash) 的設定與學習進度（這台機器的備份裡這兩個 sector 都是空的） |
41	| `0xDC000` 起 | user preset bank；CTL-1 與 fm1-base 的 app（含 Conductor）用來放面板校正 |
42	| `0xDE000` | CTL-1 的 Bluetooth 設定 |
43	| `0xE0000` | 更新時暫存 update loader |
44	| `0xF2000`–`0xF3FFF` | RemoteFM1 第一次開 Bluetooth 時寫入 |
45	| `0xFC000` | 全域設定。**SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1 都寫這裡** |
46	| `0xFE000` | SLOOP autosave 的另一份 |
47	
48	因為位址共用，韌體之間會互相踩到對方的資料，也會讀到對方留下的東西。
49	
50	## 我的機器上實際發生的 `[實機]`
51	
52	用各階段的完整備份逐 sector 比對：
53	
54	| 動作 | 改變的 sector |
55	|---|---|
56	| 原廠 015 → 裝 SLOOP 並玩過 | 韌體區，加上 `0x97000`、`0x9F000`、`0xFC000`、`0xFD000`、`0xFE000` |
57	| → Agent Deck | 韌體區，加上 `0xFC000`（蓋掉 SLOOP 的設定） |
58	| → 回 SLOOP | 韌體區，加上 `0xFE000`。曲子還在 |
59	| → CTL-1 | 韌體區，加上 `0xDE000`、`0xDF000`、`0xFC000`、`0xFD000` |
60	| → ChoralRoot | `0x04000`–`0x9EFFF`，蓋掉了 `0x97000` 的 SLOOP project（已執行，尚未用備份比對確認其他 sector） |
61	| → Conductor | 韌體區 140 個 sector（`0x04000`–`0x8EFFF`、`0x91000`–`0x91FFF`）。開機後不寫任何資料（預演 `[模擬]`；實機尚未用備份比對） |
62	
63	原廠出廠時 `0x93000`、`0xE9000`–`0xF2000`、`0xFA000`、`0xFB000` 有資料，`0xFC000`–`0xFE000` 是空的。
64	
65	## 自己比對兩份備份
66	
67	```python
68	S = 4096
69	a = open("backups/A/x.bin", "rb").read()
70	b = open("backups/B/y.bin", "rb").read()
71	print([hex(i * S) for i in range(256) if a[i * S:(i + 1) * S] != b[i * S:(i + 1) * S]])
72	```
73	
74	## 這對操作的意義
75	
76	- **只重裝韌體會保留資料區**，所以 SLOOP ↔ Agent Deck 來回曲子還在。
77	- **韌體比較大的（ChoralRoot、V16）會吃掉資料區**，回去時要還原備份。
78	- **共用的 `0xFC000` 每換一次就被蓋一次**，各韌體的全域設定不會跨韌體保留。
79	- **原廠音色在 `0xEA000`–`0xFBFFF`**，有些韌體會寫這一段。只有原廠備份救得回來。
80	- 更完整的後果見[變磚的原理與分級](../getting-started/bricking.md)與[多韌體切換](../firmware/switching.md)。
81
````
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# 自製韌體環境
2	
3	目標是把 **改 code → host simulator → fm1-emu → 批准 → 實機** 整條鏈跑通，再談功能。基礎是 [fm1-base](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base)（MPL-2.0，beta）：它在 felucca-bsp 之上提供螢幕、按鍵、LED、音訊、MIDI、storage，以及跑同一份 app 的 host simulator。
4	
5	**狀態（2026-11-17）：host simulator、實機套件 build、fm1-emu 兩種晶片開機都已跑通；還沒刷進實機。**
6	
7	## 結構
8	
9	```text
10	third_party/fm1-base/      git submodule（它自己再帶 felucca-bsp 於 bsp/）
11	firmware/hello/            fm1-base template 的原樣複本，用來驗證整條鏈
12	firmware/conductor/        agent 控制台（見 Conductor 頁）
13	firmware/morse/            摩斯電碼機（見摩斯電碼機頁）
14	firmware/common/           app 之間共用的模組（hostlink、ledfx、chime）
15	firmware/<app>/            之後的 app
16	tools/jieli/               JieLi toolchain（gitignore）
17	tools/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK/    JieLi AC79 SDK，固定 tag（gitignore）
18	```
19	
20	這符合上游的建議：把 `template/` 複製到自己的 repo，fm1-base 放在旁邊當 submodule。`tools/build.py APP_DIR` 接受任意位置的 app 目錄。
21	
22	## 指令
23	
24	| 指令 | 作用 | 我跑過嗎 |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| `just fw-setup` | 初始化 submodule、安裝 Python 工具（`fw` dependency group） | 是 |
27	| `just fw-test [app]` | build host simulator 並跑 `tests/basic.txt`，產出截圖與 WAV 到 `firmware/<app>/build/host/` | 是，全部 `ok` |
28	| `just fw-toolchain` | 下載 JieLi toolchain 與 AC79 SDK 到 `tools/`（約 1.2 GB） | 是 |
29	| `just fw-build [app]` | build 實機套件 `firmware/<app>/build/*.fwsc` | 是，約 17 秒，產出 `template.fwsc`（616 KB，identity `FM-1_1100`） |
30	
31	## 前置需求（macOS）
32	
33	- `uv`、`just`、Xcode command line tools（`cc`）。
34	- **`brew install libraqm`。** fm1-base 的字型產生器（`tools/gen_font.py`）用到 OpenType features，需要 Pillow 帶 libraqm。macOS 的 Pillow wheel 編譯時沒有包含它（`HAVE_RAQM = False`），所以 `pyproject.toml` 設了 `no-binary-package = ["pillow"]`，讓 Pillow 從原始碼對 Homebrew 的 libraqm 編譯。沒裝的話 `gen_font.py` 會報 `not supported without libraqm`。`[實機]` host 端
35	- 實機 build 另外需要 **Docker**：JieLi toolchain 只有 Linux x86-64，`build.py` 在 macOS 上會自動把每個工具放進 `linux/amd64` 容器執行。
36	
37	## 兩段式 build
38	
39	| | Host simulator | 實機套件 |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| 指令 | `build.py APP --host` | `build.py APP` |
42	| 需要 | 本機 C 編譯器 | JieLi toolchain + AC79 SDK + Docker |
43	| 產出 | `build/host/<name>_host` | `build/<name>.fwsc` |
44	| 用途 | 日常迭代、邏輯與畫面測試 | 模擬器與實機 |
45	
46	Host simulator 讀一份腳本（`tests/basic.txt`）注入按鍵與 MIDI、檢查狀態、存截圖與音訊。這是讓 agent 自己驗證改動的主要手段，不需要任何硬體。
47	
48	## Build 結果
49	
50	`just fw-build hello` 的輸出（2026-11-17）：app 226,264 B；RAM code 9,296 / 32,768 B；`.data+.bss` 76,452 / 98,304 B；build 自帶的檢查全部 `ok`（沒有 soft-double、register 存取只在 felucca-bsp 內）。
51	
52	在 fm1-emu 開機 `[模擬]`：
53	
54	| 晶片 | 結果 |
55	|---|---|
56	| `uc25hq80` | 開機到 TEMPLATE 畫面，5 秒內 12 次 flash erase / program |
57	| `p25q80` | 同上，12 次 |
58	
59	兩種晶片行為一致。這只是開機與寫入次數，「改設定 → 重開 → 讀回」還沒做。
60	
61	!!! note "之前卡住的地方"
62	    第一次 build 失敗是因為 Docker daemon 的 proxy 連不上，拉不到 `debian:bookworm-slim`（`build: cannot start the toolchain container`）。修好 Docker 的網路後就正常。遇到同樣訊息先查 `docker pull --platform linux/amd64 debian:bookworm-slim` 能不能成功。
63	
64	## 預設的 template 帶 Bluetooth
65	
66	`firmware/hello/fm1.toml` 是 `ble = true`，會用到 SDK 裡 JieLi 的 Bluetooth library（binary only）。如果第一次 build 想降低變數，可以加 `--no-ble`（產出 `NAME-usb.fwsc`）。
67	
68	## Release 與另開 repo 的問題
69	
70	fm1-base template 附的 release workflow（透過共用的 [zvenson/fm1-build](https://github.com/zvenson/fm1-build) 產生 build attestation，Firmware Hub 才會標 built from source）假設的是**獨立的 firmware repo**：app 在 `app/`、fm1-base 在 `base/`、根目錄有 `./build.sh`。放在這個筆記 repo 的子目錄不符合那個配置，所以我把複本裡的 `.github/` 拿掉了。
71	
72	結論：在本機迭代、刷自己的機器，子目錄就夠。**等某個 app 要正式 release 時，再把它搬到獨立 repo，並以 submodule 引回這裡。**
73	
74	## 自製韌體的規則
75	
76	寫在 `AGENTS.md`，重點：
77	
78	1. 先 `just fw-test`，再用 `just emu-run` 在**兩種晶片**各跑一次，才提實刷。
79	2. 存檔只走 fm1-base 的 storage 層，它處理新舊晶片的 JEDEC ID。不自己寫 flash 位址。
80	3. 自製韌體每一次實刷都要我批准，和裝別人的韌體一樣。
81	4. build 產物不進 git。
82	
83	## 下一步
84	
85	- [x] 跑通 `just fw-build hello`
86	- [x] `just emu-shot firmware/hello/build/template.fwsc` 兩種晶片都開機
87	- [ ] `just emu-run firmware/hello/build/template.fwsc` 兩種晶片各一次，改設定、重開、確認保存
88	- [ ] 批准後刷進實機，按鍵 → USB MIDI → host 端 `mido` 腳本收得到
89	- [ ] 開第一個自己的 app：最小的 MIDI controller / macro pad（按鍵送 MIDI、螢幕顯示 layer）
90	- [x] 依 [Agent Deck 試用](../firmware/agent-deck/index.md)的心得，決定 agent 控制台是 fork Agent Deck 還是在 fm1-base 上重寫：**在 fm1-base 上重寫**，見 [Conductor](../agentic/conductor.md)（`firmware/conductor`，共用模組在 `firmware/common`）
91
````

 `./docs/hardware/flash-chips.md`

```text
1	# 兩種 Flash 晶片
2	
3	2026 年後期出貨的 FM-1 換了 flash 晶片。硬體規格幾乎一樣，真正的差別在韌體相容性與救援風險。
4	
5	| | 早期 FM-1 | 2026 年後期起 |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| 型號 | Puya **P25Q80H** | UCUN **UC25HQ80** |
8	| JEDEC ID | `0x856014` | `0xB36014` |
9	| M-Flasher 顯示 | `0x856014 (old)` | `0xB36014 (new)` |
10	| 容量 | 1 MiB | 1 MiB |
11	| 介面 | SPI NOR | SPI NOR |
12	
13	沒有證據顯示新晶片讓合成器變快、音色變多或音質變好。`[調研]`
14	
15	## 為什麼換一顆 flash 會出問題
16	
17	基本的讀取、erase、page program 指令兩者相容。問題出在韌體的晶片辨識：舊程式只認得 Puya 的 JEDEC ID，遇到 `0xB36014` 就當成未知晶片而拒絕寫入。
18	
19	實際出現過的結果：
20	
21	| 現象 | 後果 |
22	|---|---|
23	| 韌體不認得 JEDEC ID | 存 preset、project 失敗 |
24	| 只存到 RAM | 關機後音色與 project 消失 |
25	| update loader 不認得新晶片 | 無法更新到修正版 |
26	| bootloader 不完全相容 | 可能無法開機，需要低階救援 |
27	
28	SLOOP 2.8.5 的 release note 寫的就是這件事：新晶片的機器「存檔與更新現在可以用了，之前被當成未知晶片」。
29	
30	## 買之前能知道嗎
31	
32	不能。目前沒有可靠的公開型號或 SKU 可以在購買前判斷。有社群回報新機螢幕下方印有 M-VAVE logo，但那不是經過驗證的對應關係，不能只靠外觀、顏色或購買日期判斷。`[調研]`
33	
34	可靠的方法只有一個：拿到機器後用 M-Flasher 進 download mode 讀 `FLASH CHIP`。這是讀取操作，不需要先刷任何東西。見[備份原廠與確認晶片](../getting-started/backup-and-chip.md)。
35	
36	## 各韌體對新晶片的支援
37	
38	| 韌體 | 新晶片 | 依據 |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| 原廠 | 正常 | 出廠即如此 |
41	| SLOOP 2.8.5 | 支援 | `[上游]` release note |
42	| Clipper 1.3.1 | 支援 | `[調研]` |
43	| Melodee 1.6.1 | 支援 | `[調研]` |
44	| m-bootloader 2.4 | 測試很少，有啟動失敗回報 | `[上游]` README |
45	| Agent Deck | 沒找到明確的實機驗證 | `[調研]` |
46	| 其他 | 未知，自己確認 | — |
47	
48	韌體在模擬器裡能開機，不代表存檔、更新與實機都沒問題。
49	
50	## 常見說法對照
51	
52	有一支介紹新舊晶片的影片（[FM-1 New VS Old Flash Chip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VNFZqDnTFYs)）。我看的是 Gemini 的摘要，不是影片本身，所以以下是 `[調研]` 對 `[上游]` 的比對。
53	
54	| 影片的說法（摘要） | 和上游一致嗎 |
55	|---|---|
56	| 螢幕下方的 logo 不能判斷晶片，有 logo 的也可能是舊晶片 | 一致。唯一可靠的是 M-Flasher 讀 `FLASH CHIP` |
57	| 新舊晶片硬體規格相同，差別只在晶片 ID | 一致 |
58	| 在 Firmware Hub 篩選支援新晶片的韌體 | 一致。見 [The Firmware Hub](../firmware/hub.md)。影片說 157 款相容、73 款不相容；我 2026-11-17 從目錄算到 152 與 71（另有 5 個不檢查晶片） |
59	| 不支援的韌體通常改兩行程式碼就能相容 | 合理。問題就是 JEDEC ID 的白名單 |
60	| 新晶片刷到不支援的舊韌體「可能導致設備損壞」 | **說得太重。** 上游與 Hub 描述的後果是存檔只留在 RAM、關機消失，以及之後的更新可能失敗，不是硬體損壞。麻煩在於可能卡在那個韌體上，要靠 download mode 救回來 |
61	| 無論新舊晶片都建議裝 bootloader 來防變磚 | **和上游不一致。** 見下 |
62	
63	### 「裝 bootloader 防變磚」為什麼不適用我這台
64	
65	這句話有一半是對的：m-bootloader 讓「韌體刷壞」之後能從按鍵進 recovery，不必靠額外硬體，這是真的保護。
66	
67	但安裝它本身就是對 boot 區的寫入，而 m-bootloader 作者自己在 README 寫：新晶片測試很少，一台裝完無法啟動、原因不明，另一台正常，結論是 `0xB36014` 的機器 install it at your own risk。影片的「無論新舊都建議裝」沒有帶這個保留。
68	
69	所以它防的是一種磚（韌體壞掉），代價是冒另一種磚（bootloader 壞掉）的風險；後者在新晶片上還沒有足夠的資料，而且只有 USB_KEY 能救。對舊晶片機，裝它是合理的。對我這台，維持[暫緩](../watch.md)。
70	
71	另外，沒有 m-bootloader 也不是毫無退路：SLOOP 與 Agent Deck 執行中都能由 M-Flasher 透過 USB MIDI 切進 download mode，Dinghy / Felucca 系的韌體按住 `OCT-` 開機有自己的 USB rescue。`[實機]` 前者我已實際用過多次。
72	
73	## 可以先在模擬器試
74	
75	fm1-emu 能模擬新晶片：網址加 `?chip=uc25hq80`，或本機 `fm1-live --flash-chip uc25hq80`。只認得 Puya 的韌體在那個模式下會把存檔留在 RAM。做一樣的操作（改音色、Save、重開）比較兩種晶片，就能在刷機前抓到一部分問題。見 [fm1-emu 模擬器](../agentic/emulator.md)。
76	
77	## 如果拿到新版
78	
79	不需要為此退換貨。只是順序要保守：先完整備份、確認目標韌體支援新晶片，m-bootloader 先不要裝。
80
```
</details></tool-use>

The s-macke/SAM repository has no formal open-source license. Its README says the author cannot put the code under a specific open-source license and that it should be used at your own risk. As long this is the case I cannot put my code under any specific open source software license Use it at your own risk. The repo is a C port of the 1982 Commodore 64 speech software, published in the year 1982 by Don't Ask Software (now SoftVoice, Inc.).

Downstream projects repeat this position:
- **zam** (a Java reimplementation) says because the copyright status of the original work remains unresolved, no specific open-source license can be granted for this project — consistent with the position taken by the upstream C reimplementation.
- **earlephilhower/ESP8266SAM** says its own wrapper code is his, but the SAM software is a reverse-engineered version of a software published more than 34 years ago by "Don't ask Software".The company no longer exists.
- Some wrappers do list permissive licenses. The Godot gdsam plugin lists MIT, but that covers its own wrapper, not the underlying SAM code.

I only ran one search and did not open the s-macke repository's license file directly, so this rests on the README excerpts and third-party descriptions.

1	# 摩斯電碼機（Morse）
2	
3	把 FM-1 變成隨身的摩斯電碼機：琴鍵當電鍵發報、即時解碼成文字、琴鍵當字母鍵盤把文字播成摩斯、用閃卡隨身練習，也能接電腦和 [Vail](https://vailmorse.com/) 跟網路上的人互傳。韌體在 `firmware/morse/`，電腦端在 `host/morse/`，都是 MIT。
4	
5	**狀態（2026-11-18）：機器上是韌體 0.2（00:14 刷入）。0.1 時已在實機確認發報、解碼、TYPE、PRACTICE、和電腦連線；0.2 的 RHYTHM、KEY 三種顯示、TYPE、LISTEN、PRESET 本人試過覺得不錯，升級後學習進度也還在 `[實機]`。韌體 0.3（修 TYPE 鍵上點劃的排版）、host 0.3.0 已在模擬器驗證，還沒刷。** 操作方式見[操作速查](morse-cheatsheet.md)。

15	相近的作品：SPELLBOX 把琴鍵當 A–Z 鍵盤；MIDIMON（fm1-base）同時當 BLE peripheral、central 與 USB host，作者說用它來 debug 另一台 FM-1。設計時參考的是其他平台的摩斯機：[Morserino-32](https://github.com/oe1wkl/Morserino-32)（模式分類、收發用不同音高）、[LCWO](https://lcwo.net/)（Koch 順序）、Vail（MIDI 格式）。只參考做法，沒有複製程式碼。
16	
17	## 功能
18	
19	| 頁面 | 做什麼 | 版本 |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| **PRACTICE** | 開機直接進來。一回合 20 張閃卡（10–30 可調），幾分鐘做完 | 0.1 |
22	| **LISTEN** | 一直播下去：你開放的 Koch 字組、常用英文字、QSO 範例、縮寫和意思、諺語。可以顯示正在播的字，或隱藏起來當抄收練習 | 0.2 |
23	| **KEY** | 自由發報：琴鍵是電鍵，解出來的字、你的速度、dah:dit 比例、字內停頓。三種顯示：TEXT（字）、CODE（每個字下面是你實際打的點劃）、TIMING（每一下照實際長短畫成條） | 0.1；顯示方式 0.2 |
24	| **RHYTHM** | 練長短：只打 dit、只打 dah、交替、SOS、自由按。每一下和目標長度比對，給提示和建議的發報速度 | 0.2 |
25	| **TYPE** | 琴鍵是字母，`OCT-`／`OCT+` 翻三頁：字母、數字和符號、片語。鍵上可以顯示點劃；LIVE（按一個字送一個）或 COMPOSE（打好一行再送） | 0.1；翻頁、片語、COMPOSE 0.2 |
26	| **CHART** | 像五十音表的字表，依熟練度上色 | 0.1 |
27	| **SETTINGS** | 速度組合（PRESET）、聽的速度、間隔、發報速度、音高、keyer（直鍵、iambic A、iambic B）、paddle 左右、聲音、每回合張數、學習方式、TYPE 的排列 | 0.1；PRESET、發報速度 0.2 |
28	
29	電鍵有兩種：**直鍵**是任一琴鍵按下就發；**iambic paddle** 是左半邊琴鍵（F3–F4）發 dit、右半邊（F#4–G5）發 dah，兩邊同時按會交替（squeeze）。Mode B 會記住在一個 element 中途按的另一邊，放開後補發一個。
30	
31	聲音是兩個 sine voice：自己發的用設定的音高（預設 600 Hz），收到的高一個大三度，聽得出是誰在發。靜音時所有琴鍵的燈會跟著節奏亮（自己發的全亮、收到的半亮），畫面上也有一條燈號。
32	
33	## 速度：WPM 是什麼、該設多少 { #speed }
34	
35	WPM 是每分鐘幾個字，以 PARIS 這個字（50 個單位）為準：**dit 的長度 = 1200 ÷ WPM 毫秒**。摩斯沒有規定一定要多快，重要的是比例：
36	
37	| 元素 | 長度 |
38	|---|---|
39	| dit | 1 單位 |
40	| dah | 3 單位 |
41	| 字裡面的停頓 | 1 單位 |
42	| 字和字之間 | 3 單位 |
43	| 字詞之間 | 7 單位 |
44	
45	| WPM | dit | dah | 大概是 |
46	|---|---|---|---|
47	| 5 | 240 ms | 720 ms | 很慢，看得清楚每一下 |
48	| 10 | 120 ms | 360 ms | 新手手打 |
49	| 13 | 92 ms | 277 ms | 以前美國業餘無線電 General 考試的速度 |
50	| 20 | 60 ms | 180 ms | Koch 建議的字元速度 |
51	| 25 | 48 ms | 144 ms | 熟練的通聯 |
52	
53	0.2 起分成兩個速度（0.1 只有一個）：
54	
55	- **聽的速度**（K1，加上 K2 的間隔）：FM-1 播給你聽的速度。Koch 的做法是字本身用 20 WPM 左右播，聽起來是一整個聲音；字和字之間用 **Farnsworth** 拉開（例如「20/8」是字用 20 WPM，整體像 8 WPM），讓你有時間想。
56	- **發報速度**（K4）：你手打的速度，用來設定 iambic keyer 的節奏、解碼器的起點、RHYTHM 頁和 TIMING 檢視的目標長度。新手的手通常比耳朵慢，所以這個要另外設低一點。
57	
58	**推薦的組合**（SETTINGS 最上面的 PRESET，轉的時候畫面會說明）：
59	
60	| PRESET | 聽 | 發 | 適合 |
61	|---|---|---|---|
62	| START（預設） | 20/8 | 10 | 剛開始 |
63	| BUILDING | 20/13 | 13 | 認得大部分的字之後 |
64	| QSO | 22/18 | 18 | 能和人一般通聯 |
65	| FAST | 25/25 | 22 | 熟練 |
66	
67	自己調的方法：到 TYPE 頁按幾個字聽聽看，轉 K1、K2 找到「字聽得出是一整個聲音、字和字之間來得及想」的組合；發報速度到 RHYTHM 頁打幾組 dit，它會依你的 dit 平均長度建議一個 K4 值。這些組合是我依 Koch／Farnsworth 的做法和常見的考試、通聯速度整理的建議 `[調研]`，不是哪個教材的固定值。
68	
69	## 學習：閃卡和間隔複習
70	
71	體驗參考背單字和學五十音：
72	
73	- **一個字兩張卡**：「認得它」（聽到或看到，說出是哪個字）和「打得出它」（看到字母，用電鍵打出來）。
74	- **Leitner 盒**：每張卡在 0–5 號盒。答對升一盒，答錯回 0 號，盒 n 每 2ⁿ 個回合複習一次。答錯的卡會在同一回合最後再問一次，這次答對也不升盒。
75	- **用回合數，不用日期**：FM-1 沒有關機後還在走的時鐘，所以排程數的是「做了幾回合」。之後接電腦時可以讓 host 送日期，改成真正的天數，但還沒做。
76	- **新字按 Koch 順序**（LCWO 的 41 字：K M U R E S N A P T L W I . J Z = F O Y , V G 5 / Q 9 2 H 3 8 B ? 4 7 C 1 D 6 0 X），5 個一組，像五十音的一「行」。一回合最多 3 個新字，每個新字先播兩次給你聽，然後才考。開著的字全部「認得」到 2 號盒以上、「打得出」到 1 號盒以上，才開下一組。
77	- **先選擇，後回想**：「認得」的卡在 0–2 號盒是聽完從四個裡選（四個選項對應 E4 F4 G4 A4 四個亮燈的鍵，干擾選項挑碼型相近的），3 號盒以上改成聽完直接打出來。
78	- 回合結束顯示答對、答錯、升了幾盒，以及連續幾回合正確率 80% 以上（streak）。中途按 `HOME` 離開，已答的部分照樣存。
79	
80	### 先用聽的：學習方式設定 { #by-sound }
81	
82	**預設是「SOUND」**：出題只用聲音，畫面上**不畫點劃**，字表只顯示熟練度，靜音時燈號照真實節奏閃，也不畫成 ·−。
83	
84	原因：Koch 法、LCWO、CW Academy 這類教學都主張把每個字的聲音當成一個整體記，不要看點劃圖。看圖學的人聽到訊號時會先數幾點幾劃再查表，速度常卡在每分鐘 10–15 字，之後得花時間改掉。`[調研]`（這是教學界的普遍說法，我還沒找到量化研究。）同樣的理由，字元速度預設 20 WPM，用 Farnsworth 把字和字之間拉開到有效 8 WPM，而不是把每個字放慢。
85	
86	這是「學認字」的規則。「練發報」時看自己打出的長短是有用的回饋，所以 KEY 頁的 CODE／TIMING 檢視、RHYTHM 頁、TYPE 頁的「鍵上點劃」都和這個設定分開，用的時候自己打開。
87	
88	「SIGHT」是另一個選項：顯示點劃，閃卡在低盒號時用「看碼選字」，KEY 頁畫出正在打的碼。切過去時畫面會提示「SOUND FIRST IS FASTER LATER」。
89	
90	| | SOUND（預設） | SIGHT |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| 認得的卡，0–2 號盒 | 聽 → 四選一 | 看點劃 → 四選一 |
93	| 認得的卡，3 號盒以上 | 聽 → 打出來 | 聽 → 打出來 |
94	| 打得出的卡 | 看字母 → 打出來 | 同左 |
95	| 靜音時認得的卡 | 看燈號節奏 → 四選一 | 看點劃 → 四選一 |
96	| 畫面上的點劃 | 不顯示 | 新字、答案、KEY 頁、字表都顯示 |
97	
98	## 練長短：RHYTHM 頁 { #rhythm }
99	
100	給還分不出長短的人。每按一下，畫面會畫出目標長度的框和你實際按的長度，顏色是綠（好）、黃（偏了）、紅（變成另一種了），並寫出「DIT 1.3（130 MS）A BIT LONG」這樣的數字：1.3 表示是目標 dit 的 1.3 倍。
101	
102	| 練習 | 目標 |
103	|---|---|
104	| DITS | 五個 dit |
105	| DAHS | 五個 dah |
106	| DIT DAH | 交替三次 |
107	| SOS | `... --- ...` |
108	| FREE | 自由按，看每一下被當成什麼 |
109	
110	判斷標準（以發報速度的 dit 為 1）：dit 在 0.5–1.5 算好、1.6–2.0 偏長、超過 2.0 就會被當成 dah；dah 在 2.2–4.0 算好、低於 1.8 會被當成 dit；1.6–2.1 是兩邊都不像的「中間地帶」。最近 16 下的平均會產生一條提示：dit 太長（附上適合你的 K4 速度）、dah 太短或太長、字內停頓太長（超過 1.8）、長短不穩（平均差 0.3 個 dit 以上）、或「GOOD RHYTHM」。
111	
112	## 收聽：LISTEN 頁 { #listen }
113	
114	一直播下去，適合放著聽。播的內容都是韌體裡現場組出來的，沒有使用任何人的教材：
115	
116	| 節目 | 內容 |
117	|---|---|
118	| KOCH GROUPS | 你已經開放的字，隨機五個一組，一行五組 |
119	| WORDS | 最常用的 100 個英文字，一行六個 |
120	| QSO | 兩個隨機呼號從 CQ、報訊號和名字、地點，到 73、`<SK>` 結束，六行一輪 |
121	| ABBREVIATIONS | 一個縮寫播兩次，畫面顯示意思（例如 QTH：my location is） |
122	| SAYINGS | 英文諺語，加上 1844 年第一封電報 WHAT HATH GOD WROUGHT |
123	
124	`SEQ` 切換「顯示」和「隱藏」。隱藏時只看得到播到第幾個字，這一行播完、下一行開始時才顯示答案，等於抄收練習；`SEL` 可以偷看。更長的教材可以從電腦用 `just morse-send -` 把文字一行一行送進來播，例如 Project Gutenberg 上公有領域的書。
125	
126	被動地一直聽能幫忙熟悉聲音，但教學上普遍認為主動抄收、回打進步比較快 `[調研]`，所以 LISTEN 是 PRACTICE 的補充。
127	
128	## 片語、prosign 和實際的用法 { #phrases }
129	
130	業餘無線電用摩斯通聯（QSO）時，有一套固定的縮寫和 **prosign**。prosign 是幾個字母連在一起當成一個符號打，中間沒有字間停頓，寫成 `<SK>` 這樣。TYPE 頁第三頁的 27 個片語鍵：
131	
132	| 片語 | 意思 | 片語 | 意思 |
133	|---|---|---|---|
134	| CQ | 呼叫任何電台 | GM / GE | 早安 / 晚安 |
135	| DE | 這裡是 | FB | fine business：很好 |
136	| K | 換你說 | R | 收到 |
137	| `<KN>` | 換你說，只限你 | QRZ? | 誰在呼叫我？ |
138	| `<AR>` | 訊息結束 | QSL | 我確認收到 |
139	| `<SK>` | 通聯結束 | `<BK>` | 換手（back to you） |
140	| `<BT>` | 停頓、換段 | HW? | 收得清楚嗎？ |
141	| 73 | 祝好、再見 | PSE | 請 |
142	| TU | 謝謝 | AGN | 再一次 |
143	| RST | 訊號報告 | QRS | 請發慢一點 |
144	| 5NN | 599 報告的簡寫 | QTH | 我的位置是 |
145	| NAME | 我的名字是 | OP | 操作員 |
146	| UR | 你的 | ES | 和 |
147	
148	**實際上大家怎麼用**：大部分人仍然是**用手即時發**（直鍵或 paddle），對方**用耳朵抄**，這是這項技能的核心。另外也很常見：
149	
150	- 電腦或「CW 鍵盤」：先打好字放在緩衝區，機器用固定速度送出，一邊送一邊還可以繼續打（type-ahead）。
151	- 比賽軟體：用 F 鍵送 `CQ TEST`、報告這類事先寫好的片語（macro）。
152	- 收的一方：有人用軟體解碼（fldigi、CW Skimmer，比賽和 Reverse Beacon Network 大量使用），但通聯本身多半還是靠人耳。`[調研]`
153	
154	TYPE 頁的 LIVE 對應「打一個送一個」，COMPOSE 對應「先打好再送」，片語鍵對應 macro。
155	
156	## 和 Vail 搭配 { #vail }
157	
158	單字、呼號、Q code、QSO 模擬、長篇抄收、和人互傳，這些深度訓練交給 Vail，不在韌體裡重做。FM-1 接上電腦就是一個 Vail 認得的 MIDI 電鍵：
159	
160	- **格式** `[上游]`：channel 1、note 0 是「已經排好時序的按鍵」，按下 `90 00 7F`、放開 `80 00 00`（[vail-adapter 的 MIDI spec](https://github.com/Vail-CW/vail-adapter/blob/master/docs/MIDI_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md)）。FM-1 的 iambic keyer 在機器上就把時序排好，所以一律送 note 0。
161	- **Vail 網頁怎麼讀** `[上游]`：[vail_web_repeater](https://github.com/Vail-CW/vail_web_repeater) 的 `static/scripts/inputs.mjs` 把 note 0 當直鍵；它只看指令（note on / note off），**不看 velocity**，所以 `90 00 00` 在 Vail 會被當成按下。我們放開一律送 `80 00 00`。Vail 打開頁面時會對所有 MIDI 輸出送 `B0 00 00`、`B0 01 xx`、`C0 xx`（給 Vail adapter 的設定），FM-1 會忽略。
162	- **Vail 的訓練工具** `[上游]`：[training.vailmorse.com](https://training.vailmorse.com/) 有 Vail CW School（進度統計、遊戲）、Hear It Type It、Send Practice（明寫支援 USB CW key 和 MIDI adapter）、Free Practice、Morse Mailbox（和朋友非同步互傳）、QSO Simulator 等。
163	- **驗證狀態**：位元組在 host simulator 和 fm1-emu 都確認過 `[模擬]`；**還沒有實際在瀏覽器裡用 FM-1 開 Vail 測過。**
164	
165	## 電腦端（host）
166	
167	`host/morse/`（Python，mido + python-rtmidi），協定見 [`host/morse/PROTOCOL.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1/blob/main/host/morse/PROTOCOL.md)：
168	
169	| 指令 | 做什麼 |
170	|---|---|
171	| `just morse-type` | 在 FM-1 的 KEY 頁發報（或在 TYPE 頁打字），解出的字打進 Mac 目前的視窗。要給終端機 Accessibility 權限；`--dry-run` 只印出來 |
172	| `just morse-send 文字` | FM-1 把文字當成「收到的」播出來，用來練抄收。`-` 從 stdin 一行一行送 |
173	| `just morse-sim` | 不接 FM-1，用文字模擬 |
174	
175	解碼在 FM-1 上做，host 只收結果（`T_CHAR`），所以畫面上看到的和打進電腦的一定一樣。host 每收到一次 HEARTBEAT 就回一個 HELLO_ACK；FM-1 超過 10 秒沒收到 host 的東西就當成斷線。
176	
177	## 兩台互傳
178	
179	現況和選項見[接口與連線](../hardware/io.md#two-units)。這台軟體的設計是**線路上傳按鍵動作（note on / off），不傳文字**，收的一方自己解碼，像真的電報線。好處是同一套格式可以走 USB、兩種藍牙 stack、USB host、經電腦轉送，Vail 也聽得懂。
180	
181	我手上只有一台，所以直連排在下一版（見[路線圖](#roadmap)），先用電腦和 Vail 跟人互傳。
182	
183	## 設計
184	
185	### 時序
186	
187	- **1 kHz tick**（`APP_TICK`，timer interrupt）：讀琴鍵 → keyer → 開關 sidetone 的 gate、送 MIDI、讀 MIDI in，按鍵變化連同時間戳放進 ring buffer。main loop 解碼、跑頁面和閃卡、畫畫面。
188	- **Sidetone 的抖動**：gate 每個 audio block 讀一次（256 frames = 5.8 ms），按下到出聲最多差一個 block。
189	- **琴鍵的 debounce**：按下約 1–2 ms 後看到、放開約 9 ms 後看到，所以直鍵的每個 mark 會被量長約 7 ms（fm1-base `bsp/boards/fm1/fm1_input.h`）。韌體在實機 build 時從直鍵的 mark 扣掉 7 ms 再解碼。fm1-emu 裡看到的是按下 +3 ms、放開 +10 ms，和預期一致 `[模擬]`。
190	- **解碼器**：分別追蹤 dit、dah 和字間間隔的平均，取中間當門檻，所以跟得上偏離設定 ±30% 的發報速度，也能讀 Farnsworth 拉開的間隔（單元測試：5／15／25／35 WPM 加 ±20% 抖動全對）。0.2 起，同一個字裡出現兩下長度差 2 倍以上時，會直接把它們當成一個 dit 一個 dah，並回頭修正前一下的判斷：新手太慢的 dit 被當成 dah，遇到第一個真正的 dah 就會改回來。但如果手打得比發報速度慢很多，連字裡的停頓都會超過切字的門檻，所以發報速度還是要設得接近你的手。
191	- **實機上看到的** `[實機]`：手打的 O（三個 dah）一次被讀成 M + T，因為 dah 之間停了 146、175 ms，和那次字與字之間的 169–224 ms 一樣長；字裡面的間隔應該只有一個 dit。另一次 dah 之間 124、133 ms 就讀對。也看到一次 9 ms 的按鍵彈跳：解碼器扣掉 debounce 偏差後當成雜訊忽略，但 MIDI 照送（Vail 會看到一下極短的按下）。
192	
193	### 存檔 { #flash }
194	
195	一筆紀錄（設定 + 學習進度，約 280 bytes）放在 `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF`，透過 fm1-base 的 storage 層存（A/B 兩份、CRC）。在回合結束或離開、改設定 3 秒後才寫。不碰 SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1 共用的 `0xFC000`。這台機器所有備份的 `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF` 都是空的。
196	
197	0.2 沿用 0.1 的紀錄格式：0.1 留下的空位改放 KEY／TYPE／LISTEN 的顯示選項、發報速度、LISTEN 的節目。從 0.1 升級時設定和進度都保留，發報速度從 0 補成預設的 10（fm1-emu 兩種晶片驗證過 `[模擬]`）。
198	
199	預演 `[模擬]`：把 `firmware/morse/build/morse.fwsc` 疊在 `backups/2026-11-17-2052-pre-conductor/` 上開機、改一個設定、玩完一回合：
200	
201	| | sector |
202	|---|---|
203	| 安裝（和目前機上的 Conductor 不同的部分） | `0x04000`–`0x1EFFF`，27 個；套件映像範圍是 `0x04000`–`0x92FFF` |
204	| 執行時寫入 | `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF`，只有這 2 個 |
205	
206	### 大小
207	
208	`just fw-build morse`（2026-11-17）：
209	
210	| 版本 | app | `.data+.bss` |
211	|---|---|---|
212	| 0.1 | 109,508 B | 27,180 / 98,304 B |
213	| 0.2 | 127,712 B | 28,444 / 98,304 B |
214	| 0.3 | 127,880 B | 28,444 / 98,304 B |
215	
216	上限是 581,564 B；RAM code 5,100 / 32,768 B；套件 616,003 B，identity `FM-1_1300`。這兩版都沒有開藍牙；加上 own BLE stack 和 central 大約再多 55–70 KB，仍然很寬裕。
217

The search didn't turn up a direct bytes-per-word figure for Talkie, but several sources give related numbers.

- **Speak & Spell data size:** One source says about 300 recorded words and phrases fit in the Speak & Spell's 32 KB ROM, and that the format is LPC-10. Dividing 32 KB by 300 gives roughly 100 bytes per word on average. That is my own estimate, not a figure from the sources.
- **Typical Talkie footprint:** A blog post on LPC speech with Talkie says a single word or phrase takes a few hundred bytes or less, so a few kilobytes of flash can hold a fair amount of speech.
- **Library contents:** The Talkie repository lists vocabulary files with sizes given in kilobytes of speech data, such as a 48K-byte US male vocabulary of 402 aeronautics words. That works out to roughly 120 bytes per word, though the page doesn't state a per-word figure itself.
- **Chip support:** Talkie emulates the TMS5220 chip. The Adafruit fork adds support for the Speak & Spell's TMS5100 chip, which requires switching the library into TMS5100 mode before using Speak & Spell vocabulary.

The official Arduino Library Manager entry for Talkie describes it as generating speech from a fixed vocabulary encoded with LPC, and it includes over 1,000 words of speech data.

```text
1	# Morse wire protocol
2	
3	Between `firmware/morse` on the FM-1 and the host (`host/morse`). Two layers, both
4	over USB-MIDI (fm1-emu's virtual cable works the same):
5	
6	1. **Keying** — MIDI notes, the [Vail adapter's format](https://github.com/Vail-CW/vail-adapter/blob/master/docs/MIDI_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md),
7	   so Vail and any MIDI tool understand it without our host.
8	2. **Text** — our own SysEx frames, for the host program only.
9	
10	## Keying (notes)
11	
12	| Direction | Message | Meaning |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| device → host | `90 00 7F` | key down (channel 1, note 0) |
15	| device → host | `80 00 00` | key up |
16	| host → device | `9n kk vv` (channel 1, any note, `vv` > 0) | received key down |
17	| host → device | `8n kk vv`, or `9n kk 00` | received key up |
18	
19	- The device sends its own keying on the **KEY** page (after its keyer: paddles come out
20	  already timed, as note 0) and what it plays on the **TYPE** page. Not on the practice
21	  pages.
22	- Up is always `80 00 00`, never `90 00 00`: Vail's web app reads the command nibble only
23	  (`static/scripts/inputs.mjs` in Vail-CW/vail_web_repeater), so a note-on of velocity 0
24	  would be a key-down there.
25	- Received keying is played on the second voice (a major third up) and decoded into amber
26	  text. Vail's CC and program change messages (`B0 00 xx`, `B0 01 xx`, `C0 xx`, sent to
27	  every MIDI output when its page opens) are ignored.
28	
29	## Text (SysEx)
30	
31	Every frame is `F0 7D 4D 4F <ver> <type> <payload…> F7`. `7D` is the MIDI non-commercial
32	ID; `4D 4F` ("MO") keeps it apart from fm1-base's `7D 4C …` and Conductor's `7D 43 4E`.
33	`ver` is 1. Payload bytes are 7-bit; text is ASCII.
34	
35	### Device → host
36	
37	| Type | Name | Payload |
38	|---|---|---|
39	| `41` | HELLO | `ver`, firmware major, minor, transport (0 USB, 1 BLE). Once a second until a HELLO_ACK |
40	| `42` | HEARTBEAT | `ver`, transport. Once a second after a HELLO_ACK |
41	| `43` | CHAR | ASCII: what the device read from the key (KEY page), or what was typed (TYPE page: a letter, or from firmware 0.2 a phrase such as `<SK> `, several characters in one frame; in COMPOSE mode the whole line when it is sent). `20` (space) ends a word; `*` is a pattern that is no character |
42	
43	### Host → device
44	
45	| Type | Name | Payload |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| `01` | HELLO_ACK | `ver`. The answer to HELLO **and to every HEARTBEAT**: the device counts the host as gone 10 s after its last frame |
48	| `02` | TEXT | ASCII, at most 60 characters: played as received, at the device's hearing speed. Characters without a code are skipped. From firmware 0.2, characters between `<` and `>` are run together as one prosign (`<SK>` is `...-.-`) |
49	| `03` | STOP | stop playing the received text |
50	
51	CHAR is sent only while the host counts as present (it answered within 10 s).
52	
53	## Shared vectors
54	
55	The same bytes are in `host/morse/protocol.py` (`VECTORS`) and in
56	`firmware/morse/tests/basic.txt`; `host/tests/test_morse.py` checks they match.
57	
58	| Name | Bytes |
59	|---|---|
60	| hello (firmware 0.3, USB) | `F0 7D 4D 4F 01 41 01 00 03 00 F7` |
61	| hello_ack | `F0 7D 4D 4F 01 01 01 F7` |
62	| char_k | `F0 7D 4D 4F 01 43 4B F7` |
63	| text_cq | `F0 7D 4D 4F 01 02 43 51 F7` |
64	| stop | `F0 7D 4D 4F 01 03 F7` |
65	
66	## Versions
67	
68	The protocol byte changes only for an incompatible change. A new frame type is gated on
69	the firmware version the HELLO reports.
70
```

The search didn't turn up official RAM or flash figures for arduino-espeak-ng on ESP32.

- **The library itself:** The README describes it as a port of eSpeak NG to Arduino, with examples including a "recommended" espeak-arduino sketch and a functional espeak example. The repo was last pushed in July 2024. eSpeak NG uses formant synthesis, which lets many languages fit in a small size. It needs to load configuration data from an espeak-ng-data directory.
- **Related pschatzmann projects:** His arduino-SAM page lists memory requirements measured on an ESP32 at about 225,000 bytes of program memory and 14,000 bytes of dynamic memory, but that is a different library. The arduino-flite page says its memory needs depend very much on the selected voice. Its ESP32 measurement for the minimal voice was about 2.34M program memory and 16,632 bytes dynamic memory. The author also noted that all voices are exceeding the possibilities of most microcontrollers.
- **A third-party project:** A Hackster.io project using arduino-espeak-ng reported moving character voice data into PSRAM and PROGMEM on an AtomS3R. That suggests the voice data is large enough to need external memory, but the post gives no figures.

For exact numbers, check the library's wiki or the docs linked from the README, or compile the espeak-arduino example for your target board and read the size report.

1	/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
2	/* learn: flash cards for Morse, the way a phrasebook or a kana deck works. Each character has two cards, recognise
3	 * it (hear it, or see its code, and name it) and send it (see it, key it), each in a Leitner box 0..5: right moves
4	 * it up a box, wrong sends it back to 0, and box n comes back every 2^n rounds. The FM-1 has no clock that lives
5	 * through a power-off, so the schedule counts rounds, not days.
6	 *
7	 * New characters come in Koch order (LCWO's), five at a time like a kana row; the next five open once every open
8	 * character is in box 2 or higher to recognise and box 1 or higher to send. No platform, no libc (tests/morse_test.c).
9	 *
10	 * Two ways to learn (LN_VISUAL): by sound, the default, where nothing shows the dots and dashes (Koch, LCWO and CW
11	 * Academy teach each character as one sound: read off a picture, it gets counted, and copying stalls around 10-15
12	 * WPM), and by sight, where the code is drawn too. Muted, the sound way shows the lamp flashing in the code's own
13	 * rhythm instead of a drawing. */
14	#pragma once
15	#include <stdint.h>
16	
17	#define LN_N 41u                         /* characters in the course */
18	#define LN_GROUP 5u                      /* opened at a time */
19	#define LN_TOP 5u                        /* the highest box */
20	#define LN_NEW_MAX 3u                    /* new characters in one round at most */
21	#define LN_CARDS_MAX 48u                 /* cards in a round, with the ones asked again */
22	#define LN_NEVER 0xFFFFu
23	
24	enum { LN_REC, LN_SEND, LN_NDIR };
25	enum {
26	    CARD_NEW,                            /* a new character: shown and played, nothing asked */
27	    CARD_HEAR_CHOOSE,                    /* hear it, pick it from four */
28	    CARD_HEAR_KEY,                       /* hear it, key it back */
29	    CARD_SEE_KEY,                        /* see the letter, key its code */
30	    CARD_CODE_CHOOSE,                    /* see the dots and dashes drawn, pick from four (by sight only) */
31	    CARD_LIGHT_CHOOSE,                   /* watch the lamp flash its rhythm, pick from four (muted, by sound) */
32	    CARD_NTYPES
33	};
34	
35	typedef struct {
36	    uint16_t round;                      /* rounds finished */
37	    uint16_t streak;                     /* rounds in a row at 80 % or better */
38	    uint8_t open;                        /* characters open, from the start of the order */
39	    uint8_t rsv;
40	    uint8_t box[LN_N][LN_NDIR];
41	    uint16_t last[LN_N][LN_NDIR];        /* the round it was last answered in; LN_NEVER: not yet */
42	    uint32_t answered, right;            /* since the start */
43	} ln_state_t;
44	
45	typedef struct {
46	    uint8_t ch, dir, type;               /* ch: index in the order */
47	    uint8_t again;                       /* asked again after a miss (once) */
48	    uint8_t opt[4];                      /* the four to choose from (indexes), for the CHOOSE types */
49	    uint8_t right;                       /* which of them is right */
50	} ln_card_t;
51	
52	typedef struct {
53	    ln_card_t card[LN_CARDS_MAX];
54	    uint8_t n, at;                       /* cards in the round, the one asked now */
55	    uint8_t ok, miss, up, fresh;         /* this round: right, wrong, moved up a box, new characters */
56	    uint32_t rng;
57	} ln_round_t;
58	
59	char ln_char(uint32_t i);                /* the character at index i of the order */
60	int ln_index(char c);                    /* its index, -1 when not in the course */
61	void ln_init(ln_state_t *s);
62	int ln_valid(const ln_state_t *s);       /* 1 when a loaded record makes sense */
63	int ln_due(const ln_state_t *s, uint32_t i, int dir);   /* this card is due this round (new ones count) */
64	uint32_t ln_due_count(const ln_state_t *s);
65	uint32_t ln_new_count(const ln_state_t *s);   /* open characters not seen yet */
66	#define LN_MUTED 1u                      /* ln_build's flags: no card that needs sound */
67	#define LN_VISUAL 2u                     /* learning by sight: drawn codes allowed */
68	int ln_choose(int type);                 /* a card answered by picking one of four */
69	/* a round of n cards (n <= LN_CARDS_MAX / 2: room for the ones asked again) */
70	void ln_build(const ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, uint32_t n, uint32_t flags, uint32_t seed);
71	const ln_card_t *ln_card(const ln_round_t *r);   /* the card asked now, 0 when the round is over */
72	/* the answer to the card asked now (ignored for CARD_NEW, which only marks the character seen): returns 1 if it

74	int ln_answer(ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, int right);
75	/* the round is over (or left): counted, the streak, and the next group opened when the open ones are learnt.
76	 * Returns 1 when a group opened */

The search didn't turn up measured RAM or CPU figures for Codec2 decoding at 700, 1200, or 3200 bps on an STM32F4 or the SM1000. It did surface some related material.

- **Design target:** One document describes Codec 2 as needing modest CPU (a few 10s of MIPs) and memory (a few 10s of kbytes of RAM), so it can run on STM32-class chips with a hardware FPU. This is a secondary, uploaded document, so treat it as a rough target rather than a benchmark.
- **STM32F4 support in the repo:** The main Codec2 repository has an stm32 directory with STM32F4 microcontroller and SM1000 FreeDV Adaptor support. Its unit-test README says the test measures CPU load and memory on an STM32F4 board, though that page's excerpt is for the 700D receive path, not 700, 1200, or 3200 bps decoding specifically.
- **700-mode caveat:** A mailing-list thread reports that one user found an #ifndef that blocked MODE_700 on STM32 because CORTEX_M4 could not be defined. A maintainer replied that the code was old and predated 700 support to the SM1000, so the 700 mode's STM32 status depends on code version.
- **3200 bps fork:** A separate fork focused on the 3200 bps mode eliminates all persistent dynamic memory allocation (no runtime malloc/free), which matters for embedded RAM use.

To get exact numbers, check the `stm32/` directory and its README in the official drowe67/codec2 repository, or run the unit tests on your own board.

15	        c = (char)(c - 32);

25	    s->round = 0;
26	    s->streak = 0;
27	    s->open = LN_GROUP;
28	    s->rsv = 0;
29	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
30	        for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++) {
31	            s->box[i][d] = 0;
32	            s->last[i][d] = LN_NEVER;
33	        }
34	    s->answered = s->right = 0;
35	}
36	
37	int ln_valid(const ln_state_t *s)
38	{
39	    uint32_t i, d;
40	    if (s->open < LN_GROUP || s->open > LN_N || s->right > s->answered)
41	        return 0;
42	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
43	        for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++)
44	            if (s->box[i][d] > LN_TOP || (s->last[i][d] != LN_NEVER && s->last[i][d] > s->round))
45	                return 0;
46	    return 1;
47	}
48	
49	static uint32_t ln_rand(uint32_t *x)     /* xorshift32 */
50	{
51	    uint32_t v = *x ? *x : 1u;
52	    v ^= v << 13;
53	    v ^= v >> 17;
54	    v ^= v << 5;
55	    return *x = v;
56	}
57	
58	int ln_due(const ln_state_t *s, uint32_t i, int dir)
59	{
60	    if (i >= s->open)
61	        return 0;
62	    if (s->last[i][dir] == LN_NEVER)     /* sending starts once it was recognised; a new character is not "due" */
63	        return dir == LN_SEND && s->box[i][LN_REC] >= 1u;
64	    return (uint32_t)(uint16_t)(s->round - s->last[i][dir]) >= (1u << s->box[i][dir]);
65	}
66	
67	uint32_t ln_due_count(const ln_state_t *s)
68	{
69	    uint32_t i, n = 0;
70	    for (i = 0; i < s->open; i++)
71	        n += (uint32_t)ln_due(s, i, LN_REC) + (uint32_t)ln_due(s, i, LN_SEND);

73	}
74	
75	uint32_t ln_new_count(const ln_state_t *s)
76	{

80	    return n;
81	}

83	/* recognising: pick from four first, recall it later. By sound it is always heard (muted: the lamp's rhythm); by
84	 * sight the first boxes show the code drawn, then it is heard */
85	static uint8_t ln_type(int dir, uint32_t box, uint32_t flags)
86	{
87	    if (dir == LN_SEND)
88	        return CARD_SEE_KEY;
89	    if (flags & LN_MUTED)
90	        return (flags & LN_VISUAL) ? CARD_CODE_CHOOSE : CARD_LIGHT_CHOOSE;

94	}

96	int ln_choose(int type) { return type == CARD_HEAR_CHOOSE || type == CARD_CODE_CHOOSE || type == CARD_LIGHT_CHOOSE; }

98	static uint32_t ln_alike(uint32_t a, uint32_t b)   /* how alike two characters' codes are */
99	{
100	    uint8_t ca = mo_code(ln_char(a)), cb = mo_code(ln_char(b));
101	    uint32_t la = mo_len(ca), lb = mo_len(cb), k, s = la == lb ? 3u : 0u;
102	    for (k = 0; k < la && k < lb; k++)
103	        s += mo_elem(ca, k) == mo_elem(cb, k);

105	}
106	
107	static void ln_options(const ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, ln_card_t *c)
108	{
109	    uint32_t pool = s->open < 4u ? 4u : s->open, score[LN_N], i, k, pick[3];
110	    for (i = 0; i < pool; i++)
111	        score[i] = i == c->ch ? 0u : 1u + ln_alike(c->ch, i) * 4u + ln_rand(&r->rng) % 6u;
112	    for (k = 0; k < 3u; k++) {
113	        uint32_t best = 0;
114	        for (i = 1; i < pool; i++)
115	            if (score[i] > score[best])
116	                best = i;
117	        pick[k] = best;
118	        score[best] = 0;
119	    }
120	    c->right = (uint8_t)(ln_rand(&r->rng) % 4u);
121	    for (i = 0, k = 0; i < 4u; i++)
122	        c->opt[i] = (uint8_t)(i == c->right ? c->ch : pick[k++]);
123	}

125	static void ln_add(const ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, uint32_t ch, int dir, uint32_t flags)
126	{
127	    ln_card_t *c;
128	    if (r->n >= LN_CARDS_MAX)
129	        return;
130	    c = &r->card[r->n++];
131	    c->ch = (uint8_t)ch;
132	    c->dir = (uint8_t)dir;
133	    c->again = 0;
134	    c->type = ln_type(dir, s->box[ch][dir], flags);
135	    c->right = 0;
136	    c->opt[0] = c->opt[1] = c->opt[2] = c->opt[3] = (uint8_t)ch;
137	    if (ln_choose(c->type))
138	        ln_options(s, r, c);
139	}
140	
141	void ln_build(const ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, uint32_t n, uint32_t flags, uint32_t seed)
142	{
143	    uint8_t qch[LN_N * LN_NDIR], qdir[LN_N * LN_NDIR], used[LN_N][LN_NDIR];
144	    uint32_t key[LN_N * LN_NDIR];
145	    uint32_t nq = 0, i, d, j, fresh = 0, first;
146	    r->n = r->at = r->ok = r->miss = r->up = r->fresh = 0;
147	    r->rng = seed ? seed : 0x9E3779B9u;
148	    if (n > LN_CARDS_MAX / 2u)
149	        n = LN_CARDS_MAX / 2u;
150	    if (n < 4u)
151	        n = 4u;
152	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
153	        used[i][0] = used[i][1] = 0;
154	    /* new characters: each shown first, then asked */
155	    for (i = 0; i < s->open && fresh < LN_NEW_MAX; i++)
156	        if (s->last[i][LN_REC] == LN_NEVER) {
157	            ln_add(s, r, i, LN_REC, flags);
158	            r->card[r->n - 1u].type = CARD_NEW;
159	            qch[nq] = (uint8_t)i, qdir[nq] = LN_REC, key[nq] = 0, nq++;

161	            fresh++;
162	        }
163	    first = nq;
164	    /* the due ones, lowest box and longest waiting first; then the weakest of the rest, to fill the round */
165	    for (j = 0; j < 2u; j++)
166	        for (i = 0; i < s->open; i++)
167	            for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++) {
168	                uint32_t wait;
169	                if (used[i][d] || (j == 0u) != (ln_due(s, i, (int)d) != 0))
170	                    continue;
171	                if (j == 1u && s->last[i][d] == LN_NEVER)
172	                    continue;            /* not yet seen, not yet due: a later round */
173	                wait = s->last[i][d] == LN_NEVER ? 0u : (uint16_t)(s->round - s->last[i][d]);
174	                qch[nq] = (uint8_t)i;
175	                qdir[nq] = (uint8_t)d;
176	                key[nq] = j * 0x10000000u + s->box[i][d] * 0x100000u + (0xFFFFu - (wait > 0xFFFFu ? 0xFFFFu : wait)) * 16u
177	                          + ln_rand(&r->rng) % 16u;
178	                used[i][d] = 1;
179	                nq++;
180	            }
181	    for (i = first + 1u; i < nq; i++) {  /* by key, new ones kept first */
182	        uint32_t k = key[i];
183	        uint8_t c = qch[i], dd = qdir[i];
184	        for (j = i; j > first && key[j - 1u] > k; j--) {
185	            key[j] = key[j - 1u];
186	            qch[j] = qch[j - 1u];
187	            qdir[j] = qdir[j - 1u];

189	        key[j] = k, qch[j] = c, qdir[j] = dd;
190	    }
191	    if (nq > n)
192	        nq = n > first ? n : first;
193	    for (i = nq; i > 1u; i--) {          /* asked in a shuffled order */
194	        uint32_t k = ln_rand(&r->rng) % i;
195	        uint8_t c = qch[i - 1u], dd = qdir[i - 1u];
196	        qch[i - 1u] = qch[k], qdir[i - 1u] = qdir[k];
197	        qch[k] = c, qdir[k] = dd;
198	    }
199	    for (i = 0; i < nq; i++)

205	int ln_answer(ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, int right)
206	{

208	    uint8_t *box;

242	}
243	
244	int ln_finish(ln_state_t *s, const ln_round_t *r)
245	{
246	    uint32_t i, asked = r->ok + r->miss;
247	    if (!asked)
248	        return 0;
249	    s->round++;
250	    if (r->at >= r->n)                   /* a whole round: the streak; one left halfway does not change it */
251	        s->streak = r->ok * 100u >= asked * 80u ? (uint16_t)(s->streak + 1u) : 0u;
252	    if (s->open >= LN_N)
253	        return 0;
254	    for (i = 0; i < s->open; i++)
255	        if (s->box[i][LN_REC] < 2u || s->box[i][LN_SEND] < 1u)
256	            return 0;
257	    s->open = (uint8_t)(s->open + LN_GROUP > LN_N ? LN_N : s->open + LN_GROUP);
258	    return 1;
259	}
260	
261	uint32_t ln_level(const ln_state_t *s, uint32_t i)
262	{
263	    if (i >= LN_N)
264	        return 0;
265	    return (s->box[i][LN_REC] + s->box[i][LN_SEND]) / 2u;
266	}
267

搜索结果里没有直接涉及杰理(JieLi)SDK 提示音格式、`wtg`/`f1a` 文件结构或其 ADPCM 解码实现的内容。我找到的都是间接相关的资料:

- **ADPCM 基础**:Unity 文档把 ADPCM 描述为一种解码成本低、但会引入额外噪声瑕疵的压缩格式。该压缩格式解码成本低,但与其他压缩类型相比,它包含额外的噪声瑕疵。 阿里云的文章则介绍了它的编解码原理,即每个 16 位采样以 4 位存储。它将声音流中每次采样的 16bit 数据以 4bit 存储,所以压缩比 1:4.
- **ADPCM 算法实现**:意法半导体(ST)的应用笔记 AN2931 讲解了在 STM32 上实现 ADPCM 编解码器的方法,包括编码和解码函数的结构。本应用笔记描述了 ADPCM 音频固件编解码器,并提供了演示固件来说明如何在使用STM32F103xxI2S 时,利用外部的 DAC 来播放 ADPCM 文件。 它的目录里有 ADPCM_Decode 函数一节,可以作为理解解码逻辑的参考,但它不是杰理的格式。
- **提示音转换流程的类似案例**:安凯微(Ai-Thinker)VB590 的文档描述了一套把提示音 WAV 文件转换成 C 源文件(beep.c/beep.h)并加入 SDK 编译的流程。本文档实现了提示音的 WAV 文件转为 beep.c 和 beep.h,beep.c 和 beep.h 再放到 CDK 的 SDK 里去做编译。 这说明同类芯片 SDK 通常需要专用工具先转换提示音,但它不是杰理的工具链。

建议的后续搜索方向:用"杰理 提示音 工具""AC69 提示音 转换""JieLi 提示音 ADPCM 解码"等关键词,或直接查看杰理官方 SDK 文档与开发者社区(如 Gitee 或博客上的 SDK 解析文章)。

1	/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
2	/* tone: see tone.h */
3	#include "tone.h"
4	
5	#define TONE_RATE 44100.0f
6	#define TONE_RAMP (1.0f / (0.005f * TONE_RATE))   /* 5 ms from silent to full */
7	#define TONE_AMP 0.3f
8	
9	static struct {
10	    volatile uint8_t gate;
11	    volatile float inc;                  /* phase step per frame, of a turn */
12	    float phase, ramp;                   /* ramp 0..1, shaped into the level */
13	} tone_v[TONE_N];
14	static volatile uint8_t tone_muted;
15	
16	void tone_pitch(int v, float hz)
17	{
18	    if (v >= 0 && v < TONE_N)
19	        tone_v[v].inc = hz / TONE_RATE;
20	}
21	
22	void tone_gate(int v, int on)
23	{
24	    if (v >= 0 && v < TONE_N)
25	        tone_v[v].gate = (uint8_t)(on != 0);
26	}
27	
28	void tone_mute(int on) { tone_muted = (uint8_t)(on != 0); }
29	
30	int tone_gated(int v) { return v >= 0 && v < TONE_N && tone_v[v].gate; }
31	
32	void tone_stop(void)
33	{
34	    uint32_t v;
35	    for (v = 0; v < TONE_N; v++) {
36	        tone_v[v].gate = 0;
37	        tone_v[v].ramp = 0.0f;
38	    }
39	}
40	
41	void tone_render(int32_t *lr, uint32_t n, float gain)
42	{
43	    uint32_t v, i;
44	    for (v = 0; v < TONE_N; v++) {
45	        float inc = tone_v[v].inc, phase = tone_v[v].phase, ramp = tone_v[v].ramp;
46	        int on = tone_v[v].gate;
47	        if (!on && ramp <= 0.0f)
48	            continue;
49	        for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
50	            float lvl, s;
51	            ramp += on ? TONE_RAMP : -TONE_RAMP;
52	            ramp = ramp < 0.0f ? 0.0f : ramp > 1.0f ? 1.0f : ramp;
53	            phase += inc;
54	            if (phase >= 1.0f)
55	                phase -= 1.0f;
56	            if (tone_muted)
57	                continue;
58	            lvl = ramp * ramp * (3.0f - 2.0f * ramp);   /* smoothstep: the ramp's corners rounded */
59	            s = fm_sinf(phase * 6.2831853f) * lvl * TONE_AMP * gain;
60	            lr[2 * i] += (int32_t)s;
61	            lr[2 * i + 1] += (int32_t)s;
62	        }
63	        tone_v[v].phase = phase;
64	        tone_v[v].ramp = ramp;
65	    }
66	}

1	# fm1-base
2	
3	A base for M-VAVE FM-1 firmware, on [felucca-bsp](https://github.com/hugelton/felucca-bsp): the platform layer
4	above the hardware (screen, drawing and fonts, panel, LEDs, audio, MIDI over USB and TRS, storage, the screen reader),
5	a host simulator and a browser emulator that run the same app, and the tools to build, package and install it.
6	MPL-2.0: an app built on it may use any licence. See [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md), [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md) and
7	[CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).
8	
9	**Status: beta.** Two firmwares are built on it so far, and they are its proof points:
10	[CTL-1](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-ctl) (with Bluetooth MIDI) and
11	[Radio](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-radio) (with WiFi). Expect the platform interface (`include/plat.h`)
12	and `fm1.toml`'s settings to change before 1.0.
13	
14	The template (`template/`) runs on an FM-1: screen, keys and their LEDs, sound, MASTER, encoders, settings kept
15	across a power cycle, USB-MIDI both ways, the screen reader, and an update started from the template itself. The same
16	app runs on the computer in the host simulator and in the browser: try the template's at
17	<https://charlesvestal.github.io/fm1-base/emu/>.
18	
19	    git clone --recursive https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base
20	
21	## Optional parts
22	
23	A firmware has only what its fm1.toml asks for (and its app.h, for velocity and pressure); every build prints the
24	parts it has.
25	
26	| Part | How to include it | What the app calls |
27	| --- | --- | --- |
28	| Bluetooth MIDI with a computer or tablet | `ble = true` (`tools/build.py --no-ble` leaves it out of one build) | `TO_BLE`, `PORT_BLE`; `plat_ble_state`, `plat_ble_connected`; `plat_ble_enable`; with `ble_stack = "own"` a stream of SysEx frames read by the radio at the link's rate (`plat_ble_stream`: a screen mirrored) and the link as agreed (`plat_ble_link_info`) |
29	| Bluetooth MIDI devices (the FM-1 connects to a keyboard or controller) | `ble_central = true`, with `ble` | `plat_ble_scan`, `plat_ble_found`, `plat_ble_connect`, `plat_ble_disconnect`, `plat_ble_device`; `TO_BLE_HOST`, `TO_BLE_DEV`, `plat_midi_in_from` (one link at a time); `plat_ble_passkey` on the own stack |
30	| Bluetooth on fm1-base's own stack instead of JieLi's libraries (below) | `ble_stack = "own"`, with `ble` | the same calls |
31	| Pairing on the own stack (LE legacy pairing, the bond kept) | `ble_pairing = true`, with `ble_stack = "own"` | nothing |
32	| Bluetooth MIDI in by the sender's time (for an app that follows a clock by time) | `ble_midi_time = true`, with `ble_stack = "own"` | `plat_midi_in_t24` after `plat_midi_in` |
33	| Bluetooth audio to headphones and speakers (A2DP) | `bt_audio = true`, with `ble_stack = "own"`; `bt_log = true` puts its set-up on the radio's log | `plat_bta_on`, `plat_bta_scan`, `plat_bta_found`, `plat_bta_known`, `plat_bta_pick`, `plat_bta_reconnect`, `plat_bta_forget`, `plat_bta_hangup`, `plat_bta_state` |

46	| Lower case in the big fonts | `font_full = ["L"]` | the fonts as ever |
47	| The firmware as an `.rfm1` for host apps (RemoteFM1 for iOS), below | `tools/build.py APP_DIR --rfm1` | nothing |
48	| The browser emulator's own parts (`tools/build.py --web`): web/emu/parts, each file saying what it does; without any, the page and app.wasm are as before. One is on without asking: `resample`, the FM-1's 44.1 kHz played at the browser's rate (many computers run audio at 48 kHz), where the page takes parts (fm1-base's page and worklet) | `emu = ["name", ...]`, `"-resample"` to leave it out (or `FM1B_EMU="name ..."` for one build: those parts only) | nothing, unless a part says so |
49	
50	Every firmware also counts each port's MIDI messages, in and out: `plat_midi_count(PORT_*, out)` for counters,
51	`plat_midi_ago` for activity lights.
52	And: `plat_midi_out_room(to)` (room in the out queues, each Bluetooth link's its own, for a sequencer's note-offs),
53	`plat_midi_in_from()` (where the last message in came from, as an out: for MIDI thru) and `plat_midi_out_link()` (a new
54	USB connection); `plat_store_size` and `plat_store_head` (an object whole or not at all; its header only); big data in
55	flash beyond the store with `plat_data*`, in the data area and two more windows (`PLAT_XDATA0`, `PLAT_XDATA1`), and a
56	third on request (`xdata2 = true`: `PLAT_XDATA2`, 0xFC000..0xFEFFF).
57	
58	## Bluetooth and WiFi
59	
60	A firmware has Bluetooth or WiFi, not both: each fills most of what the FM-1 has (the chip has no external RAM),
61	and together they don't fit. WiFi, and Bluetooth on JieLi's stack, need JieLi's AC79 SDK (`$AC79_SDK`) for its
62	libraries. Bluetooth on fm1-base's own stack (`ble_stack = "own"`) links nothing of JieLi's, and neither does a
63	build without a radio. Every build still takes the three SDK files a package needs (LICENSING.md).
64	
65	### Two Bluetooth stacks
66	
67	By default (`ble = true`), Bluetooth runs on JieLi's binary libraries from the SDK, through a shim (`ble/`). With
68	`ble_stack = "own"` it runs instead on Henri David's stack from [Optimist](https://github.com/w0ts/optimist),
69	in `bt/` under MPL-2.0, with felucca-bsp's radio drivers. Nothing of JieLi's is linked, there is no shim and no
70	task, and the build checks it. The radio calibrates itself at every start, so an FM-1 whose stock calibration was
71	overwritten works the same. The own stack is smaller and does more:
72	
73	- Bluetooth MIDI with a computer or a phone, as on JieLi's.
74	- With `ble_pairing = true` it pairs and encrypts the link (LE legacy pairing), and keeps the bond in `OBJ_BLE`.
75	  Without it a pairing is refused; macOS and iOS connect anyway.
76	- `ble_diag = false` leaves out the link layer's diagnostics (its counters and event rings: about 2.4 KB of RAM
77	  and some code; the radio log's `BT ll` line). They are kept by default.
78	- With `ble_midi_time = true` each message from Bluetooth comes with the time it was sent, from its BLE-MIDI
79	  timestamp (`plat_midi_in_t24`): the connection's bunching taken out, for an app that times a clock it follows
80	  itself. Without it the clock and transport are held to the sender's time (spaced as sent, up to 0.12 s later).
81	- With `ble_central = true` the FM-1 connects to Bluetooth MIDI devices, as on JieLi's. A device that asks for a
82	  code gets one on the FM-1's screen (`plat_ble_passkey`).
83	- With `bt_audio = true` it sends its sound to headphones and speakers (A2DP, SBC), beside Bluetooth MIDI on the
84	  one radio. While it streams, the FM-1's own output is muted. Four devices are remembered, the last one first, and
85	  `plat_bta_reconnect(0)` at power-on connects it again. `bt_log = true` adds the audio set-up's steps to the
86	  radio's log.
87	
88	It was tried on one FM-1 with a Mac, an iPhone (GarageBand; Cubasis as host and as a peripheral with the code),
89	headphones (AIAIAI TMA-2) and a speaker (Anker SoundCore 2), MIDI and audio at once. Its limits:
90	
91	- One Bluetooth MIDI link at a time: while the FM-1 is connected to a device, a computer can't connect to it
92	  (JieLi's keeps both).
93	- Audio reaches the ear 150-300 ms after a key (the device's own buffer): for listening, not for playing in time.
94	- After an abrupt drop, a speaker may not answer for a minute or two.
95	- Each firmware keeps its own keys. After switching firmware, forget the FM-1 on the phone or speaker and pair
96	  again.
97	
98	`examples/ble_own` is the template on the own stack with every option. For how the stack works, see
99	[docs/bt/README.md](docs/bt/README.md).
100	
101	### Turning Bluetooth on
102	
103	1. In fm1.toml, `ble = true`. Add `ble_central = true` for the FM-1 to connect to MIDI devices too (a keyboard,
104	   a controller), beside a computer. For the own stack, add `ble_stack = "own"` and its options (above).
105	2. In app.h, give it a store object: `OBJ_BLE` in the app's object enum, and its offset in `APP_STORE_MAP` (the
106	   radio's address and pairing are kept there). On the own stack an app may keep them in its own saved data instead
107	   (a settings record of its own): `#define APP_BLE_STORE` and `app_ble_load` / `app_ble_save` (plat.h `struct
108	   plat_ble_rec`), and no `OBJ_BLE`.
109	3. In the app: MIDI goes out with `TO_BLE` and comes in on `PORT_BLE`, as USB's does. For a page of devices, add
110	   `#define APP_BTDEV` to app.h and use lib/btdev.h (the template's REC does).
111	4. With devices there are two links, the computer's and the device's. `TO_BLE` goes to both; `TO_BLE_HOST` or
112	   `TO_BLE_DEV` goes to one, each with its own queue, so a slow device never holds up the computer. Both come in on
113	   `PORT_BLE`, and `plat_midi_in_from()` says which. MIDI thru, with nothing sent back where it came from (a keyboard
114	   played through to a phone): after each `plat_midi_in`,
115	   `plat_midi_send(pkt, (TO_USB | TO_BLE) & ~plat_midi_in_from())`.
116	
117	Bluetooth starts at every power-on, as on M-VAVE's firmware, unless the last Bluetooth run crashed. A firmware
118	that lets the player turn it off keeps that as a setting, calls `plat_ble_enable(0)` / `plat_ble_enable(1)` when it
119	changes, and tells the platform whether to start it at power-on with `APP_BLE_AT_BOOT` in app.h (an expression,
120	e.g. `(set.bluetooth != 0)`). Off ends every link and stops advertising and scanning: the radio is quiet. Its manual
121	should say where the setting is (the template's: for details, see template/docs/MANUAL.md).
122	`tools/build.py --no-ble` builds the same firmware without Bluetooth (NAME-usb.fwsc).
123	
124	### Turning WiFi on
125	
126	1. In fm1.toml, `wifi = true` (and not `ble`). Leave USB audio out (`usb_audio_in = false`, `usb_audio_out =
127	   false`): WiFi needs its RAM.
128	2. In app.h, two store objects: `OBJ_BLE` (the radio's address and calibration) and `OBJ_WIFI` (the networks
129	   kept), with their offsets in `APP_STORE_MAP`; and a smaller canvas, `#define APP_CANVAS_PX (240u * 48u)` (draw
130	   the screen in strips 48 rows high or less).
131	3. The app's network code goes in its own files, listed in fm1.toml's `net = [...]`: they're built as the SDK
132	   builds code that talks lwIP, and include `lwip/sockets.h`. That code runs in a task of its own
133	   (`plat_net_task`): a socket call waits, and the main loop must not.
134	4. In the app: `plat_wifi_on(1)` turns it on; it joins the networks it joined before (six, the most recent first).
135	   `plat_wifi_scan` and `plat_wifi_found` list the networks around, `plat_wifi_join` joins one (kept once joined),
136	   `plat_wifi_state` and `plat_wifi_ip` say how far it got. Passwords come over USB:
137	   `tools/fm1_remote.py wifi join SSID PASSWORD` (or typed on the keys: Radio has a page for it).
138	
139	For a working example, see `examples/wifi`; for a whole firmware, fm1-radio.
140	
141	### What each costs
142	
143	The FM-1 has a 581 KB app slot in the flash, 96 KB of RAM for `.data` and `.bss` (128 KB in a WiFi build), and a
144	336 KB pool of RAM for big buffers (304 KB in a WiFi build). With `ram_layout = "packed"` in fm1.toml
145	(`device/app_packed.ld`) the RAM code, `.data` and `.bss` and the pool share one budget of 464 KB instead, packed from
146	its bottom, 8 KB kept spare (and `main_stack` / `irq_stack` may give it the stacks' unused part). Measured on the
147	template (October 2026), in KB:
148	
149	| | Flash | RAM | Pool |
150	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
151	| The template without a radio (`--no-ble`) | 77 | 27 | 68 |
152	| Bluetooth MIDI with a computer (`ble`) | + 124 | + 45 | + 24 |
153	| Bluetooth MIDI devices too (`ble_central`) | + 8 | + 1 | 0 |
154	| Bluetooth MIDI with a computer on the own stack (`ble_stack = "own"`) | + 41 to 46 | + 10 | + 1 |
155	| Pairing, devices and Bluetooth audio too (`ble_pairing`, `ble_central`, `bt_audio`) | + 57 to 62 | + 8 | + 30 |
156	| WiFi (`wifi`, from fm1-radio's measurements) | + about 300 | + about 100 | + about 276 |
157	
158	- Bluetooth: JieLi's BT controller and stack (the flash), its 24 KB heap and their tables (the RAM), three task
159	  stacks of 8 KB (the pool). The template with Bluetooth and devices is 214 KB of flash, 75 of 96 KB of RAM: room
160	  for a big app (CTL-1, with a General MIDI synth, is 491 KB).
161	- The own stack: the template with Bluetooth MIDI alone is 118 to 123 KB of flash, 37 KB of RAM and 69 KB of pool;
162	  with pairing, devices and audio, 180 KB, 45 KB and 99 KB. On a big app the
163	  difference shows: LOOM-8 on JieLi's stack is 506 KB of flash, 88 KB of RAM and 327 KB of pool; on the own stack
164	  with MIDI alone, 454 KB, 68 KB and 318 KB; with pairing, devices, audio and its pages for them, 512 KB, 91 KB and
165	  328 KB.
166	- WiFi: JieLi's driver (146 KB), the WPA supplicant (77 KB), lwIP (51 KB), the radio layer, crypto and the shim
167	  (25 KB) in the flash; the driver's buffers, lwIP, the shim's task table and 24 KB of the heap (about 100 KB) in
168	  the RAM; the rest of the heap (248 KB) and lwIP's packet buffers (28 KB) in the pool. The heap, 272 KB, holds the
169	  WiFi library's own buffers (about 60 KB) and its tasks' stacks (4 to 8 KB each, by task, as a task starts: about
170	  6), and what is left is the app's (`malloc`; fm1-radio's HE-AAC player and HTTPS stream peak at 256 KB of it).
171	  That leaves an app about 170 KB of flash and a few KB of RAM.
172	  WiFi calibrates its radio at every start (a kept calibration was Bluetooth's, which the access point could not
173	  hear). `examples/wifi` is 420 KB of
174	  flash, 119 of 128 KB of RAM and 299 of 304 KB of pool; fm1-radio (MP3 and HE-AAC decoders, HTTPS) is
175	  576 KB, 127 KB and 300 KB.
176	- In a WiFi build, fm1-base's large font (the splash's name, the panel's screens) can go too:
177	  `#define APP_BIG_FONT FONT_M` in app.h saves 20 KB of flash.
178	- An app with fonts of its own can give them to fm1-base's screens (crash, safe mode, update, restore,
179	  calibration, the splash): `#define APP_SYS_TEXT` in app.h and its `app_sys_h`, `app_sys_w`, `app_sys_text`
180	  (`device/sys_text.c`); fm1-base's faces are then left out (LOOM-8: 18 KB).
181	
182	## Development over USB
183	
184	`tools/fm1_remote.py` drives an FM-1 running any fm1-base firmware as a player would: buttons, keys, encoders,
185	MASTER, and reads back what the screen says (the screen reader's channel), the last crash and the radio's log; with
186	WiFi, it turns it on and off, joins networks and reads its state (`wifi ...`).
187	For example, `tools/fm1_remote.py listen tap REC wait 3000 screen log`.
188	It finds the FM-1 as the web pages do (`tools/fm1ports.py`, the same rules as `web/fm1ports.js`): a port with an
189	FM-1's usual name, or else one that answers the screen reader's HELLO, whatever it is called; `--port NAME` picks one.
190	`tools/fm1_install.py`, `fm1_backup.py`, `fm1_mirror.py` and `fm1_debug.py` find it the same way.
191	
192	The site's installer page (`tools/make_site.py`, from `web/installer.html`) reads the same crash record and log in
193	Chrome or Edge: "Report a problem" shows them, ready to copy, so a player can send them without Python. The record
194	survives a restart, not switching off.
195	
196	The pages find the FM-1 with `web/fm1ports.js`, under any port name: a port with one of the FM-1's usual names, one
197	the player picked (Try), or one that answers the screen reader's HELLO, which every fm1-base firmware does. Only the
198	HELLO goes to other ports, three times: its ID, 7D, is the one for non-commercial use, which other gear ignores.
199	The [FM-1 Screen Reader](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-reader)'s page uses the same file, as a copy.
200	
201	The screen reader's firmware side lives here too: `device/announce.c` and `tools/gen_words.py` (MPL-2.0, like the
202	rest; see LICENSING.md) are the one copy. fm1-reader keeps the page, the voice, the protocol (its PROTOCOL.md), the audit and the skill, and its
203	`tools/sync_announce.sh` copies these two files into the firmwares not on fm1-base.
204	
205	## .rfm1: your firmware in host apps
206	
207	An `.rfm1` file is your firmware built to run inside an app instead of on the FM-1: RemoteFM1 for iOS first, as
208	an instrument or an AUv3. It is the host simulator compiled to WebAssembly, the same app as on the FM-1, with a
209	manifest (name, version, licence, the source at its commit), your credits and the licence texts. Users download it
210	from your release and put it in the app's firmware folder. The format is RemoteFM1IOS's
211	[docs/RFM1-FORMAT.md](https://github.com/Quixotic7/RemoteFM1IOS/blob/main/docs/RFM1-FORMAT.md).
212	
213	    tools/build.py APP_DIR --rfm1                    # APP_DIR/build/rfm1/ID-dev+COMMIT.rfm1 (emcc, as --web)
214	    tools/build.py APP_DIR --rfm1 --release X.Y      # APP_DIR/build/NAME-X.Y.rfm1, beside NAME-X.Y.fwsc
215	
216	The ID is fm1.toml's `name` in lower case. Without `--release` the version is `dev+` and the app repository's commit.
217	The template's release workflow builds the release's `.rfm1` and attests it with the package.
218	The manifest's `source_url` is fm1.toml's `repo` at that commit, so commit (and push) what you build. Its `license`
219	is fm1.toml's `licence`, and its authors are `authors = ["..."]` or the repository's first author. The memory is fixed
220	at 8 MiB (`rfm1_memory_mib`, at most 32). The build checks the module against the format before it writes the file.
221	
222	In the app, the panel, screen, LEDs, sound, MIDI both ways, velocity and pressure (`APP_TOUCH`) and the screen
223	reader (over SysEx) work as in the browser emulator. Saved objects and the data area are kept by the app with its
224	state. There is no radio, no USB host and no environment (`getenv` returns nothing). `tests/rfm1_test.mjs FILE`
225	drives a file as a host app does.
226	
227	## firmware.json: your firmware in hubs
228	
229	Every build writes `firmware.json`, a description of the firmware for the places that list and install FM-1
230	firmwares (The Firmware Hub, RemoteFM1, M-Flasher): its name, author, licence, a paragraph on it, tags, the install
231	page, and the hardware it needs (the flash parts it saves to, the parts the build has, such as Bluetooth MIDI or USB
232	audio). It comes from fm1.toml (`author`, `description`, `tags`, `install`, `site`, with the site's `tagline`, `repo`,
233	`licence` and `credits`) and lands in `APP_DIR/build/` and, for an app in `app/`, at the repository's root, to commit.
234	The format, its fields and its vocabularies are in [docs/FIRMWARE-JSON.md](docs/FIRMWARE-JSON.md).
235	
236	## Moving a Felucca-based firmware here
237	
238	A Felucca-based firmware (GPL-3.0) can move onto fm1-base and felucca-bsp and keep its licence: their MPL-2.0 files
239	may be part of a GPL work, and stay MPL-2.0 file by file. It then has the platform's parts and fixes with every other
240	firmware, instead of its own copy of Felucca. `skill/felucca-to-fm1-base/` is a Claude skill that walks through the
241	move: the inventory (what is platform, what is the app), what fm1-base needs, the port, the checks (the app's
242	scenarios compared byte for byte with the old simulator's, then the FM-1), and the licensing files. It never changes
243	the firmware's licence: it asks. Relicensing to MPL-2.0 is needed only to link JieLi's Bluetooth or WiFi libraries;
244	`skill/felucca-to-fm1-base/RULES.md` has what it takes (`tools/provenance.py` finds Felucca's lines and whose they
245	are). To move a firmware with Claude Code, run this from inside its repository (Node.js's `npx` fetches the skill
246	into the project):
247	
248	    npx degit --force charlesvestal/fm1-base/skill/felucca-to-fm1-base .claude/skills/felucca-to-fm1-base && claude "Move this firmware onto fm1-base with the felucca-to-fm1-base skill"
249	
250	Claude starts with the inventory and shows it before changing anything. To have the skill in every project instead,
251	fetch it to `~/.claude/skills/felucca-to-fm1-base`. It reads as plain instructions too, without Claude.
252
```

2	
3	FM-1 的開源 ecosystem 依用途分五層。每層一張表：連結、角色、一句評價。各韌體玩起來怎樣、怎麼選，見[韌體地圖](firmware/index.md)，這裡不重複。

5	## 「權威」在這裡的意思
6	
7	依序是三種來源：
8	
9	1. **原廠來源**：M-VAVE 的官方韌體與 SDK。
10	2. **工具作者的一手實作**：例如 M-Flasher 和 m-bootloader 的 README、release notes、原始碼。

12	
13	GitHub stars 只代表關注度，**不是刷機安全性的證據**。

23	| [jvitkauskas/m-bootloader](https://github.com/jvitkauskas/m-bootloader) | 開機前檢查韌體、recovery menu、USB MIDI 安裝與備份 | SLOOP 3 需要它；新晶片上的實機驗證少，見[注意事項](getting-started/cautions.md) |

1	# 韌體地圖
2	
3	FM-1 同一時間只跑一套主要韌體，換韌體就是重刷。可以先在 [fm1-emu 線上模擬器](https://joakimeriksson.github.io/fm1-emu/)試玩，再決定哪些值得刷進真機。
4	
5	這是依用途整理的個人選擇，不是 GitHub stars 排名。版本與查核日期見[資源地圖](../resources.md)。部分專案還在早期開發或只有有限的實機驗證，不代表每個都適合刷進日常使用的機器。
6	
7	## 音樂類
8	
9	| 韌體 | 變成什麼 | 備註 |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| [SLOOP 2.8](https://github.com/isod89/sloop-fm1) | 四軌 groovebox：3 synth + 1 drum，12 種 engine | **首選**，支援新晶片。見 [SLOOP](sloop/index.md) |
12	| [SLOOP 3](https://github.com/isod89/sloop3-fm1) | 重寫的新一代 groovebox：4 synth + 1 drum | public beta，必須先裝 m-bootloader。見 [SLOOP 3](sloop/sloop3.md) |
13	| [Melodee](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee) | 多 engine synth + sequencer，和弦與 song mode | 有 Bluetooth MIDI `[調研]` |
14	| [Clipper](https://github.com/isod89/clipper-fm1) | 偏 sound design 的實驗性合成器，源自 SLOOP | 有 web editor `[調研]` |
15	| [X0X](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-x0x) | 909、808、兩台 303 的 groovebox | techno / acid |
16	| [zp12](https://github.com/zvenson/zp12) | SP-12 風格的 lo-fi sampling 鼓機 | hip-hop |
17	| [ChoralRoot](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ChoralRootFM1) | Orchid 風格的和弦樂器：左手選和弦性質，右手彈根音 | 見 [ChoralRoot](choralroot/index.md)。從 SLOOP 切過去有已知風險 |
18	| [Felucca](https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca) | 多 engine 合成器 | 多數社群韌體的源頭與硬體層 |
19	| [FM-1 SID](https://github.com/joakimeriksson/fm1-sid) | Commodore 64 SID 合成器 | 跑在 fm1-dock 上 |
20	
21	## 想要 looper 的話
22	
23	先講限制：**FM-1 沒有音訊輸入**，所以做不到 Quantiloop 那種「錄進來的聲音疊錄」的 audio looper。FM-1 上的 looper 錄的都是它自己彈的音符或和弦，再重新發聲。要 loop 外部聲音（吉他、人聲），還是得用 iPad 上的 Quantiloop / Loopy Pro，FM-1 當音源或控制器。
24	
25	| 韌體 | looper 的性質 | 新晶片（Hub 標示） | 備註 |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| [SLOOP](sloop/index.md) | 即興疊錄的四軌 groovebox：free take 模式下不用節拍器，loop 的長度決定 tempo，可一直 overdub | 認得 | 最接近「現場 loop 一首歌」。我用過 |
28	| [ChoralRoot](choralroot/index.md) | 錄和弦的 looper：十個 slot，Overwrite / Overdub / Replace / Step 等錄音模式，播放中可換音色與 voicing | 認得 | 我現在裝的 |
29	| [Tonitor](https://github.com/nzimas/tonitor) | 六軌、**沒有 tempo 與格線**的自由長度 loop，每軌最多十層 overdub，另有 granulator。走 ambient / 實驗路線 | 認得 | Hub 上約 1,300 次安裝。作者強調它不是 groovebox。我沒試過 |
30	| [RemoteFM1](remotefm1/index.md) | 不接主機時內建一個 looper | 認得 | 附帶功能 |
31	| [fm1-chord](https://github.com/math0ne/fm1-chord) | 和弦機加 looper | **只認舊晶片** | 不要裝在我的機器上 |
32	| [PT/FM](https://github.com/hitosu/ptfm) | tracker 式的口袋工作站，含 loop station | **只認舊晶片** | 同上 |
33	
34	清單來自 Firmware Hub 目錄的描述（2026-11-17），除了 SLOOP 與 ChoralRoot 以外我都沒有實際用過。
35	
36	用法上的建議：要「打一段鼓、疊 bass、再疊和弦」這種 looper 手感，SLOOP 最合適；要自由、沒有節拍的聲音疊層，看 Tonitor；要 loop 真的聲音，用 iPad。
37	
38	## 控制器與工具類
39	
40	| 韌體 | 變成什麼 | 用途 |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| [CTL-1](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-ctl) | MIDI controller，自帶 General MIDI 音色 | 控制 DAW、外部合成器、iPad app。見 [CTL-1](ctl-1/index.md) |
43	| [Trireme](https://github.com/ignis32/trireme_fm1) | Vial 相容的 USB HID macro keyboard | 快捷鍵、桌面自動化，不需要 host daemon |
44	| [RemoteFM1](https://github.com/Quixotic7/RemoteFM1) | 把 FM-1 變成面板，韌體在電腦、手機或瀏覽器上跑 | 不重刷就換韌體。見 [RemoteFM1](remotefm1/index.md) |
45	| [Macropad Patch](https://github.com/smememe/fm1-macropad-patch) | 把原廠 V15 patch 成 MIDI macro pad | host 端自訂所有按鍵行為 |
46	| [MIDI Processor](https://midihax.github.io/fm1-midi-processor/html/index.html) | MIDI filter、remap、monitor | MIDI routing、debug `[調研]` |
47	
48	## Agent 類
49	
50	| 韌體 | 變成什麼 |
51	|---|---|
52	| [FM-1 Agent Deck](https://github.com/kevinelliott/fm-1-agent-deck) | Claude Code、Codex 等 CLI agent 的實體控制台，整合 Herdr 與 tmux |
53	
54	細節見[用 FM-1 控制 agent](../agentic/agent-deck.md)。

56	## 開發用的 base
57	
58	想自己寫韌體時的起點。這個 repo 目前還沒有建置環境。
59	
60	| 專案 | 定位 | License |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| [felucca-bsp](https://github.com/hugelton/felucca-bsp) | 基礎 BSP / HAL | MPL-2.0 |
63	| [fm1-base](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base) | BSP 之上的 platform、host simulator 與 template | MPL-2.0 |
64	| [dinghy](https://github.com/zvenson/dinghy) | 最小的可運作韌體 template | GPL-3.0 |
65	| [fm1_open](https://github.com/m-vave/fm1_open) | M-VAVE 官方開放韌體與 binary SDK | GPLv3 + SDK linking exception |
66	| [fm1-nes](https://github.com/Keitark/fm1-nes) | JieLi SDK 原生開發範例 | Apache-2.0 |
67	
68	控制器類的新專案，`fm1-base` 比直接 fork 一整套 GPL 的 Felucca / SLOOP 合適：它已處理螢幕、按鍵、MIDI、storage，而且 MPL-2.0 讓自己的應用程式可以選別的 license。它還是 beta，API 可能變動。`[調研]`
69	
70	## 怎麼選
71	
72	- 只想做音樂：SLOOP 2.8。
73	- 想接 DAW 當鍵盤 / 控制器：CTL-1。
74	- 想要 Bluetooth MIDI：留在原廠，或 CTL-1、Melodee。SLOOP 不支援。
75	- 想研究 agent 控制台：先在模擬器玩 Agent Deck，不用刷。
76	- 換韌體前先看[多韌體切換](switching.md)與[注意事項](../getting-started/cautions.md)。
77

```text
1	# The Firmware Hub
2	
3	[The Firmware Hub](https://thefirmwarehub.com/) 是目前最大的 FM-1 社群韌體目錄：列出韌體、在瀏覽器裡一鍵安裝（Chrome / Edge，Web MIDI）、連到模擬器試玩，並附救援教學。安裝不需要帳號。
4	
5	以下數字來自它的 `catalog.json`，查核於 **2026-11-17**（目錄自己標的更新時間是 2026-11-16 18:01 UTC）。`[上游]`
6	
7	## 有什麼
8	
9	FM-1 共 **228** 個韌體：
10	
11	| 類別 | 數量 |
12	|---|---|
13	| synth | 89 |
14	| groove（groovebox） | 76 |
15	| other（控制器、工具、遊戲等） | 26 |
16	| drums | 16 |
17	| tracker | 11 |
18	| chords | 8 |
19	
20	安裝次數最多的幾個：SLOOP（約 11,500）、JIANT FM、Skiff、Felucca、Melodee、OberVave、FMini-1、Clipper。很多條目是這幾個主幹的衍生版。
21	
22	除了 FM-1，Hub 也收 M-VAVE SMK-37、Elektron Model:Cycles、Erica Synths LXR-02 的韌體，並有工具區（模擬器、editor、備份與救援、自己 build）、Knowledge Base 與 creator 名單。
23	
24	## 新晶片篩選：對我這台最重要的功能
25	
26	Hub 會從每個套件裡讀出它認得哪些 flash 晶片，並提供篩選 **Saves on newer FM-1s**。我的機器是新晶片 `0xB36014`，裝東西前先看這一欄。
27	
28	| Hub 的標示 | 意思 | 數量 |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| Every FM-1, the newer chip too | 套件認得新晶片 | 152 |
31	| The first FM-1s only | 只認得舊晶片：在新機上存檔只留在 RAM，更新也可能失敗 | 71 |
32	| Every FM-1: it does not check the chip | 不檢查晶片；Hub 註明他們沒在新晶片上試過 | 5 |
33	
34	我在用或考慮過的：
35	
36	| 韌體 | Hub 版本 | 新晶片 |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| SLOOP | 2.8.5 | 認得 |
39	| Felucca | 1.8.2 | 認得 |
40	| Melodee | 1.6.1 | 認得 |
41	| Clipper | 1.3.1 | 認得 |
42	| X0X | 1.2.2 | 認得 |
43	| CTL-1 | 1.0.3 | 認得 |
44	| AGTDECK（Agent Deck） | 0.6.3 | 認得（Hub 版本比上游 release 的 0.7 舊） |
45	| SLOOP DX7 Banks、SLOOP Floyd FM、X0X-RMX、Felucca [Salt] | — | **只認舊晶片**，不要裝 |
46	
47	衍生版不一定跟上主幹：SLOOP 本身支援新晶片，但基於舊版 SLOOP 的幾個 fork 還沒有。
48	
49	!!! warning "「認得晶片」不等於「測過」"
50	    這一欄是從套件內容判讀出來的，不是實機測試結果。Hub 自己聲明它不跑測試也不做 review，只檢查檔案是不是 FM-1 套件。還是要自己備份、刷完做存檔測試。
51	
52	## 我怎麼用它
53	
54	- **找東西、看新晶片標示**：用 Hub。
55	- **下載與安裝**：仍然從韌體作者自己的 GitHub release 下載、對 digest，再用 `just fm1-flash`。這樣版本最新（例如 Agent Deck），而且寫入前有 M-Flasher 的檢查與自動備份。
56	- **試玩**：Hub 的 Try 與 [fm1-emu](../agentic/emulator.md) 是同一個模擬器。
57	- **救援教學**：Hub 的 [FM-1 rescue](https://thefirmwarehub.com/tools/rescue/) 依「你看到什麼」分步驟寫，和[救援](../getting-started/recovery.md)互補。
58	
59	Hub 上標「Built from source」的套件有 build attestation（由共用的 [zvenson/fm1-build](https://github.com/zvenson/fm1-build) 產生）。那代表檔案確實是從那個 commit build 出來的，不代表韌體安全。
60	
61	## 和 remotefm1.com、fm1-emu 的關係
62	
63	三個網站看起來功能重疊，其實是三層：
64	
65	| 東西 | 角色 | 誰做的 |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| **The Firmware Hub** | **目錄**：有哪些韌體、套件在哪、認不認得新晶片 | zvenson / Designburg |
68	| **[fm1-emu](../agentic/emulator.md)** | **模擬器引擎**：模擬 FM-1 的晶片，原封不動地跑 `.fwsc` | joakimeriksson |
69	| **[remotefm1.com](https://remotefm1.com/)（FM-1 Player）** | **播放器**：用上面兩者，再加上自己的原生執行方式與「把實機當面板」 | Quixotic7 |
70	
71	FM-1 Player 的頁面自己寫明：韌體清單來自 Firmware Hub 的即時目錄（我看到時列了 243 個）；帶圓點的韌體以 `.rfm1` 原生執行（韌體的原始碼編成 WebAssembly）；其餘每一個都能用 fm1-emu 模擬執行，套件從 Hub 指向的位置抓。`[上游]`
72	
73	所以來源確實是 Hub，模擬的部分是 fm1-emu。Hub 自己的 Try、Agent Deck 的線上展示頁、我本機的 `just emu-run` 用的也都是 fm1-emu。差別在 FM-1 Player 多了原生核心（比較快、延遲低）以及搭配 [RemoteFM1](remotefm1/index.md) 把實機當面板。
74	
75	## 官方網站
76	
77	M-VAVE 官方的產品頁與下載在 [cuvave.com](https://www.cuvave.com/product?id=fm-1)（Cuvave 是 M-VAVE 的公司網站）。官方韌體 `FM-1.fwsc` 與更新工具 M-UPGRADE 從那裡的 Download 取得。頁面內容是 JavaScript 動態載入的，我沒有逐項核對上面目前列的版本。
